question:
An organization uses an ML model to predict customer churn but has no mechanism to get direct user feedback or track when customers leave. They want to test for drift by analyzing the data being fed into the live ML model. '
Which test type would be MOST appropriate in this situation and why?
options: a) Dynamic drift testing, because it can infer the current ground truth by analyzing the input data's statistical properties
b) Static drift testing, because it identifies drift by detecting changes in the data distributions without requiring ground truth
c) Dynamic drift testing, because comparing ML model predictions to actual results is the most direct way to measure performance degradation
d) Static drift testing, because it compares the ML model's live performance metrics against a predefined acceptance threshold
answer: b) Static drift testing, because it identifies drift by detecting changes in the data distributions without requiring ground truth

explaination.b) Static drift testing, because it iden: Correct! Since ground truth (actual customer churn outcomes) is unavailable, static drift testing compares live input feature distributions against the training baseline (e.g., using Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests) without needing labels.
explaination.c) Dynamic drift testing, because compar: Incorrect! Dynamic drift testing requires actual ground truth labels, which are missing here.

question:
When testing a trained ML model, the development team found that the model was highly accurate when evaluated using validation data but performed poorly with independent test data.
Which of the following options is MOST likely to cause this situation?
options: a) Underfitting
b) Concept drift
c) Overfitting
d) Low acceptance criteria
answer: c) Overfitting

explaination.a) Underfitting: Incorrect! Underfitting yields poor performance across all datasets.
explaination.b) Concept drift: Incorrect! Concept drift happens post-deployment due to changing relationships over time.
explaination.c) Overfitting: Correct! Overfitting occurs when a model learns the training and validation data too closely (including noise), leading to poor generalization on unseen independent test data.

question: Which of the following statements BEST describes how A/B testing is used in the context of a machine learning system (MLS)?
options: a) A/B testing is primarily used to generate diverse test cases that cover all possible inputs for an MLS
b) A/B testing is used to verify that all components within an MLS interact correctly with each other
c) A/B testing determines if an updated version of an MLS performs better than the previous version
d) A/B testing focuses on analyzing the internal algorithm structure of an MLS to identify potential defects
answer: c) A/B testing determines if an updated version of an MLS performs better than the previous version

explaination.c) A/B testing determines if an updated: Correct! A/B testing deploys two versions (A and B) to live users simultaneously to compare real-world performance metrics and determine if a new model version outperforms the old one.

question: Which of the following descriptions of the creation of a pseudo-oracle used to support the back-to-back testing of an ML model is MOST likely to be CORRECT?
options: a) By varying the hyperparameters used for training the ML model that is being tested
b) By fine-tuning the ML model that is being tested
c) By supplementing the ML model that is being tested with retrieval-augmented generation
d) By using a different ML development framework than the ML model that is being tested
answer: d) By using a different ML development framework than the ML model that is being tested

explaination.d) By using a different ML development f: Correct! A pseudo-oracle in back-to-back testing can be implemented using an alternative independent implementation—such as training a model in a different framework or using a simpler baseline model—to cross-validate outputs and catch implementation bugs.

question: Which of the following BEST describes the primary focus of Machine Learning Development Testing compared to Model Testing?
options: A. Machine learning development testing focuses on evaluating the internal mathematical weights and decision boundaries of a trained neural network.
B. Machine learning development testing focuses on addressing risks introduced by development tools, configuration choices, framework APIs, and deployment mechanisms.
C. Machine learning development testing focuses exclusively on generating adversarial attack prompts for generative AI models.
D. Machine learning development testing replaces the need for data representativeness testing in the data pipeline.
answer: B. Machine learning development testing focuses on addressing risks introduced by development tools, configuration choices, framework APIs, and deployment mechanisms.

explaination.A. Machine learning development testing: Incorrect! Evaluating model quality/weights falls under Model Testing.
explaination.B. Machine learning development testing: Correct! Machine Learning Development Testing targets risks associated with the software development environment, pipelines, frameworks (e.g., PyTorch/TensorFlow APIs), toolchains, and deployment environments.
explaination.C. Machine learning development testing: Incorrect! Adversarial testing is a specific security/robustness technique, not the core scope of development testing.
explaination.D. Machine learning development testing: Incorrect! Development testing complements data pipeline testing rather than replacing it.

question: An engineering team is concerned that data leakage might occur due to an improper split between training, validation, and holdout test datasets. Which risk mitigation activity should be performed?
options: A. Model conversion testing
B. Data allocation review
C. Fuzz testing
D. Installability testing
answer: B. Data allocation review

explaination.A. Model conversion testing: Incorrect! Model conversion testing evaluates quantization and framework translation (e.g., PyTorch to ONNX).
explaination.B. Data allocation review: Correct! A Data Allocation Review examines how data is split across training, validation, and testing sets to prevent data leakage (overlap or improper stratification).
explaination.C. Fuzz testing: Incorrect! Fuzz testing inputs invalid or random data to check for crashes.
explaination.D. Installability testing: Incorrect! Installability testing verifies deployment/installation scripts.

question: When MUST Rollback Testing be executed during the deployment lifecycle of a Machine Learning System?
options: A. Only after a critical production failure has already occurred in the live environment.
B. Prior to actual deployment, to verify the system's capability to revert to a stable operational state if a deployment fails.
C. During initial data preparation before exploratory data analysis.
D. Continuously during white-box adversarial attacks.
answer: B. Prior to actual deployment, to verify the system's capability to revert to a stable operational state if a deployment fails.

explaination.A. Only after a critical production fail: Incorrect! Waiting for a live failure defeats the proactive purpose of testing.
explaination.B. Prior to actual deployment, to verify: Correct! Rollback testing must be conducted prior to release to ensure the infrastructure can safely and automatically revert to a previous baseline model if an error occurs post-deployment.

question: An AI development team converts a PyTorch model into ONNX format for deployment on mobile devices. Which test type explicitly verifies that predictive accuracy and inference speed are maintained after format conversion?
options: A. Model Conversion Testing
B. Framework Documentation Review
C. A/B Testing
D. Inter-Annotator Agreement Testing
answer: A. Model Conversion Testing

explaination.A. Model Conversion Testing: Correct! Model conversion testing explicitly assesses whether optimizing, quantizing, or converting a model from one format/framework (e.g., PyTorch) to another (e.g., ONNX, TensorRT) introduces numerical drift or performance degradation.

question: A QA manager notices that developers frequently misuse complex PyTorch API methods, introducing hidden runtime errors in model pipelines. Which testing activity directly mitigates this specific development risk?
options: A. Shadow Testing
B. API Testing
C. Kolmogorov-Smirnov Distribution Testing
D. Metamorphic Invariance Testing
answer: B. API Testing

explaination.B. API Testing: Correct! API testing in ML development focuses on verifying that the functions and interfaces of ML frameworks/libraries (like PyTorch or TensorFlow) are called correctly according to specification, handling edge cases without runtime failures.

question:
Scenario: A financial institution wants to evaluate a newly trained fraud-detection model against live operational data. However, compliance regulations strictly forbid exposing live customers to unverified model predictions until performance is proven.
Which deployment testing strategy is MOST appropriate for this scenario?
options: A. Canary Testing, because only 5% of users receive responses from the new model.
B. Shadow Testing, because the new model runs in parallel with live traffic without returning its predictions to live users.
C. Installability Testing, because it validates GPU installation scripts.
D. A/B Testing, because live traffic is randomly split 50/50 to measure conversion metrics.
answer: B. Shadow Testing, because the new model runs in parallel with live traffic without returning its predictions to live users.

explaination.A. Canary Testing, because only 5% of us: Incorrect! Canary testing still exposes a subset of real users to the new model's outputs.
explaination.B. Shadow Testing, because the new model: Correct! Shadow deployment feeds real live requests to the new model in parallel with the legacy model without sending its responses to users, allowing performance validation under real conditions without regulatory risk.
explaination.D. A/B Testing, because live traffic is: Incorrect! A/B testing serves responses to live users.

question:
Scenario: An e-commerce company wishes to release an updated product recommendation engine. The team wants a small percentage of real online buyers (e.g., 3%) to actively interact with the new model so they can monitor real-time purchase conversion rates and system latency before a full rollout.
Which deployment test approach meets this objective?
options: A. Shadow Testing
B. Canary Testing
C. Rollback Testing
D. Framework Suitability Review
answer: B. Canary Testing

explaination.A. Shadow Testing: Incorrect! Shadow testing does not return predictions to real users, preventing measurement of actual purchase conversion rates.
explaination.B. Canary Testing: Correct! Canary testing routes a small fraction (e.g., 3%) of live production traffic to the new model variant while the majority remains on the baseline, allowing measurement of real user interactions.

question:
Scenario: A computer vision model trained on cloud GPUs is quantized from 32-bit floating-point to 4-bit integer precision for deployment on low-power IoT cameras. During field testing, the camera system experiences unexpected memory crashes and reduced frame rates across different camera hardware models.
Which TWO testing types were likely omitted or inadequately performed during deployment preparation?
1. Model Conversion Testing
2. Cross-Device Testing
3. Label Correctness Testing
4. Metamorphic Testing
options: A. 1 and 2
B. 2 and 3
C. 1 and 4
D. 3 and 4
answer: A. 1 and 2

explaination.A. 1 and 2: Correct! Model conversion testing verifies quantization effects, memory usage, and performance after converting/compressing the model. Cross-device testing evaluates performance across heterogeneous physical target hardware.

question:
Scenario: A data science team runs a single training pass of a deep learning model and obtains an accuracy score of 91.2%. They immediately claim the model passes acceptance criteria. However, when the QA team retrains the model with a different random seed, accuracy drops to 82.5%.
What risk occurred, and how should it be systematically addressed according to ISTQB CTAI development testing principles?
options: A. Risk: Unacceptable Data Drift; Address by running Chi-squared tests on raw input data.

B. Risk: Incorrect interpretation of test results due to the stochastic nature of learning; Address by conducting multi-run statistical evaluation (e.g., k-fold cross-validation or bootstrap resampling) during ML functional performance testing.
C. Risk: Sub-optimal API selection; Address by rewriting PyTorch API endpoints.
D. Risk: Defective Installability; Address by updating GPU drivers.
answer: B. Risk: Incorrect interpretation of test results due to the stochastic nature of learning; Address by conducting multi-run statistical evaluation (e.g., k-fold cross-validation or bootstrap resampling) during ML functional performance testing.

explaination.B. Risk: Incorrect interpretation of tes: Correct! ML training is inherently non-deterministic (stochastic). Evaluating a single training run leads to misleading results; multi-run training, cross-validation, or seed averaging is required to quantify variance.

question:
Scenario: You are establishing a CI/CD pipeline for deploying an ML-based translation service. You need to ensure that if a new model deployment causes an immediate crash or high error rate on the server, the deployment pipeline automatically reverts to the previous stable model within 10 seconds.
Which testing process MUST be automated and validated in the CI/CD pipeline to guarantee this safety net?
options: A. Rollback Testing
B. Disparate Impact Analysis
C. Inter-Annotator Agreement Testing
D. Exploratory Prompt Testing
answer: A. Rollback Testing

explaination.A. Rollback Testing: Correct! Rollback testing explicitly verifies that the deployment mechanism can successfully detect failure and quickly revert to the previous functioning model release without service outage.

question: Which TWO of the following scenarios describe ML development risks that can be EFFECTIVELY mitigated by performing ML functional performance testing?
options: a) A team notices that their ML development framework becomes slow and even unresponsive when processing large batches of data
b) A new version of a core library used by the ML development framework appears to be causing the ML model to produce unexpected and inaccurate results
c) After a new installation, the development team needs a quick test to determine if the ML development framework’s essential services are running correctly
d) A single test result is difficult to reproduce during evaluation, showing slight variations in ML functional performance with each execution
e) A project leader needs to decide between two potential algorithms based on their suitability for the project's goals
answer: b) A new version of a core library used by the ML development framework appears to be causing the ML model to produce unexpected and inaccurate results
d) A single test result is difficult to reproduce during evaluation, showing slight variations in ML functional performance with each execution

explaination.a) A team notices that their ML developm: Incorrect! This is a performance issue of the framework itself, not the ML model's functional performance.
explaination.b) A new version of a core library used: Correct! ML functional performance testing can detect regressions or unexpected behavior caused by changes in underlying libraries or dependencies.
explaination.c) After a new installation, the develop: Incorrect! This is an installability or smoke test, not functional performance testing.
explaination.d) A single test result is difficult to: Correct! ML functional performance testing can identify inconsistencies and variations in model behavior under different conditions.
explaination.e) A project leader needs to decide betw: Incorrect! This is a decision-making scenario, not a functional performance testing scenario.

question: Which of the following statements CORRECTLY describes how shadow testing differs from canary testing in the deployment of ML models?
options: a) Shadow testing affects the responses from real users, while canary testing does not involve real users
b) Shadow testing mirrors traffic without impacting users, while canary testing provides responses from the new ML model
c) Canary testing is used for performance testing, while shadow testing is mainly used for component integration testing
d) Canary testing compares ML models running offline, while shadow testing is based on the use of live user data
answer: b) Shadow testing mirrors traffic without impacting users, while canary testing provides responses from the new ML model

explaination.b) Shadow testing mirrors traffic withou: Correct! Shadow testing replicates real production traffic to the new model in parallel without outputting its predictions to users, whereas canary testing routes a subset of actual live users to receive responses from the new model.

question: What are the characteristics of a conventional computer system?
options: 1. Learn from new data automatically
2. Based on probability to produce results
3. Execute clearly programmed rules
4. No oracle testing required
answer: 3. Execute clearly programmed rules

explaination.1. Learn from new data automatically: Incorrect! Automatic learning from data is a characteristic of AI-based systems, not conventional systems.
explaination.2. Based on probability to produce resul: Incorrect! Conventional systems operate deterministically rather than probabilistically.
explaination.3. Execute clearly programmed rules: Correct! Conventional computer systems rely on explicit, pre-programmed instructions and rules written by developers.
explaination.4. No oracle testing required: Incorrect! Oracle testing (knowing expected outputs) is typically required and feasible for conventional systems.

question: What is the main difference between AI-based systems and conventional systems?
options: 1. AI-based systems use more loops.
2. AI-based systems learn from data instead of relying solely on programming rules.
3. Conventional systems do not use data.
4. AI-based systems are always more accurate.
answer: 2. AI-based systems learn from data instead of relying solely on programming rules.

Incorrect! The fundamental difference is architectural and conceptual, not the number of loops.
explaination.2. AI-based systems learn from data inst: Correct! AI systems derive patterns and decision logic from training data rather than relying exclusively on hardcoded IF-THEN rules.
Incorrect! Conventional systems process input data; they just don't learn from it to adapt their underlying logic.
explaination.4. AI-based systems are always more accu: Incorrect! AI systems can make errors and are not universally more accurate than rule-based systems.

question: Which term describes the situation where the same input always produces the same output?
options: 1. Adaptive
2. Transparent
3. Probabilistic
4. Deterministic
answer: 4. Deterministic

explaination.1. Adaptive: Incorrect! Adaptability refers to the ability to change or learn over time.
explaination.2. Transparent: Incorrect! Transparency refers to how easily understandable a system's inner workings are.
explaination.3. Probabilistic: Incorrect! Probabilistic systems can yield varying outputs or confidence scores for the same input.
explaination.4. Deterministic: Correct! Deterministic systems guarantee that identical inputs will always produce identical, reproducible outputs.

question: An image recognition system returns: Cat = 92% Dog = 8% . What characteristics of AI are demonstrated?
options: 1. Deterministic processing
2. Probabilistic reasoning
3. Static behavior
4. Hard-coded rule execution
answer: 2. Probabilistic reasoning

explaination.1. Deterministic processing: Incorrect! Deterministic processing would yield binary or absolute fixed outcomes without confidence percentages.
explaination.2. Probabilistic reasoning: Correct! Expressing classification results as confidence percentages reflects probabilistic reasoning and output generation.
explaination.3. Static behavior: Incorrect! The output varies dynamically based on confidence levels.
explaination.4. Hard-coded rule execution: Incorrect! Image recognition models rely on learned patterns rather than hard-coded rules.

question: Why is testing AI-based systems often more difficult than testing conventional systems?
options: 1. AI has no input.
2. AI has no output.
3. AI can generate probabilistic results.
4. AI has no code.
answer: 3. AI can generate probabilistic results.

Incorrect! AI systems take inputs just like conventional software.
Incorrect! AI systems produce predictions, classifications, or generated content.
explaination.3. AI can generate probabilistic results: Correct! The probabilistic and non-deterministic nature of AI makes defining strict expected oracles and test validation much harder.
Incorrect! AI systems have underlying code, frameworks, and model weights.

question: What does "Black Box Nature" in AI mean?
options: 1. AI runs in the dark.
2. AI cannot be upgraded.
3. It is difficult to understand how AI makes decisions.
4. AI cannot be tested.
answer: 3. It is difficult to understand how AI makes decisions.

Incorrect! This is a literal misunderstanding of the term.
Incorrect! AI models can be retrained and updated.
explaination.3. It is difficult to understand how AI: Correct! The 'black box' analogy refers to the opacity of complex models (like deep neural networks), where internal reasoning paths are not easily traceable.
Incorrect! AI can and must be tested using specialized AI testing methodologies.

question: You are testing an AI system for diagnosing diseases. Which factor is most important?
options: 1. Beautiful interface
2. Explainability
3. Network speed
4. Dark mode
answer: 2. Explainability

explaination.1. Beautiful interface: Incorrect! While usability matters, it is not the most critical factor for high-stakes medical diagnoses.
explaination.2. Explainability: Correct! In critical domains like healthcare, doctors and patients must understand *why* a diagnosis was made to ensure safety, trust, and regulatory compliance.
explaination.3. Network speed: Incorrect! Speed is secondary to diagnostic accuracy and reasoning transparency.

question: Transparency and explainability are of particular interest for what reason?
options: 1. Reducing model size
2. Complying with AI-related requirements and regulations
3. Reducing data volume
4. Increasing CPU speed
answer: 2. Complying with AI-related requirements and regulations

explaination.1. Reducing model size: Incorrect! Explainability does not directly reduce model size.
explaination.2. Complying with AI-related requirement: Correct! Emerging AI regulations and ethical frameworks (e.g., EU AI Act) mandate transparency and explainability for high-risk AI applications.
explaination.3. Reducing data volume: Incorrect! Explainability does not impact data volume.
explaination.4. Increasing CPU speed: Incorrect! Explainability mechanisms can actually add computational overhead.

question: Which is an example of adaptability?
options: 1. Manually modifying source code to add new rules
2. AI improving performance with new data
3. Restarting the system
4. Running regression tests
answer: 2. AI improving performance with new data

explaination.1. Manually modifying source code to add: Incorrect! Manual code changes represent traditional maintenance, not system adaptability.
explaination.2. AI improving performance with new dat: Correct! Adaptability in AI refers to the system's ability to evolve, learn, and improve performance when exposed to new training or operational data.

question: Which of the following systems is most likely an AI-based system?
options: 1. Calculator
2. VAT calculation program based on a fixed formula
3. Facial recognition system
4. Temperature conversion program from °C to °F
answer: 3. Facial recognition system

explaination.1. Calculator: Incorrect! A calculator uses deterministic arithmetic rules.
explaination.2. VAT calculation program based on a fi: Incorrect! Uses explicit, hardcoded mathematical formulas.
explaination.3. Facial recognition system: Correct! Facial recognition relies on machine learning algorithms and pattern recognition from image data.
explaination.4. Temperature conversion program from °: Incorrect! Uses a fixed mathematical equation.

question: A tester observed that the same email was passed through an AI spam filter twice, but the probability of it being spam the first time was 91% and the second time was 89%. Which characteristic of AI-based systems does this reflect?
options: 1. Explainability
2. Determinism
3. Probabilistic behavior
4. Static rules
answer: 3. Probabilistic behavior

explaination.1. Explainability: Incorrect! Explainability relates to understanding the decision rationale.
explaination.2. Determinism: Incorrect! Determinism would mean identical probabilities on both runs.
explaination.3. Probabilistic behavior: Correct! Slight variations in probability scores across executions highlight the probabilistic and dynamic nature of certain AI models.
explaination.4. Static rules: Incorrect! AI models do not rely on static rules.

question: Which statement is TRUE?
options: 1. AI systems are always more accurate than conventional systems.
2. AI systems always have good explainability.
3. Conventional systems need to learn from data to function.
4. AI systems often learn patterns from data.
answer: 4. AI systems often learn patterns from data.

explaination.1. AI systems are always more accurate t: Incorrect! AI systems can make mistakes and hallucinate.
explaination.2. AI systems always have good explainab: Incorrect! Many advanced AI models (like deep neural networks) have very low explainability.
explaination.3. Conventional systems need to learn fr: Incorrect! Conventional systems function via programmed rules, not data learning.
explaination.4. AI systems often learn patterns from: Correct! Machine learning models build their predictive logic by discovering patterns within training datasets.

question: A conventional software system calculates shipping costs using predefined business rules. Which characteristic does this demonstrate?
options: 1. Pattern recognition
2. Statistical inference
3. Explicit rule-based processing
4. Self-learning
answer: 3. Explicit rule-based processing

explaination.1. Pattern recognition: Incorrect! Pattern recognition is typical of AI/ML systems.
explaination.2. Statistical inference: Incorrect! Statistical inference applies to probabilistic models.
explaination.3. Explicit rule-based processing: Correct! Predefined business rules executed by software represent explicit rule-based processing.
explaination.4. Self-learning: Incorrect! Self-learning applies to AI systems that update from data.

question: An AI model was trained using thousands of customer emails to classify messages as "spam" or "not spam". What is the primary source of the model's behavior?
options: 1. If-then-else statements created by developers
2. Patterns learned from training data
3. Hardcoded business logic
4. Regression test cases
answer: 2. Patterns learned from training data

explaination.1. If-then-else statements created by de: Incorrect! Developers do not write manual spam rules in a machine learning approach.
explaination.2. Patterns learned from training data: Correct! Machine learning models acquire their classification behavior by extracting statistical patterns from training email datasets.
explaination.4. Regression test cases: Incorrect! Test cases verify behavior, they do not generate it.

question: Which statement about AI-based systems is TRUE?
options: 1. They always produce identical outputs for identical inputs.
2. They rely entirely on manually coded decision rules.
3. They often use probabilistic reasoning.
4. They cannot be tested.
answer: 3. They often use probabilistic reasoning.

explaination.1. They always produce identical outputs: Incorrect! Some AI models incorporate stochastic elements or probabilistic scoring.
explaination.3. They often use probabilistic reasonin: Correct! AI models frequently evaluate inputs and assign probabilities to various outcomes.
Incorrect! They can and must be tested using specialized AI quality assurance methods.

question: A tester notices that understanding how an AI model reached a decision is very difficult. Which AI challenge is being observed?
options: 1. Scalability
2. Explainability
3. Maintainability
4. Portability
answer: 2. Explainability

explaination.1. Scalability: Incorrect! Relates to handling growing workloads.
explaination.2. Explainability: Correct! Difficulty in tracing or interpreting how an AI model arrived at a specific output is the core challenge of explainability (black box problem).
explaination.3. Maintainability: Incorrect! Relates to code modification ease.
explaination.4. Portability: Incorrect! Relates to running across environments.

question: Why are AI systems often described as "black boxes"?
options: 1. Their source code is encrypted.
2. Their outputs are hidden from users.
3. Their internal decision-making process may be difficult to understand.
4. They can only run on specialized hardware.
answer: 3. Their internal decision-making process may be difficult to understand.

Incorrect! Encryption is unrelated to the black box concept.
Incorrect! Outputs are presented to users.
explaination.3. Their internal decision-making proces: Correct! The complexity of internal weights and feature transformations makes the reasoning path opaque (black box).
explaination.4. They can only run on specialized hard: Incorrect! False; they can run on standard CPUs/GPUs.

question: Which characteristic is MOST associated with conventional systems?
options: 1. Adaptability
2. Learning from experience
3. Deterministic behavior
4. Continuous model improvement
answer: 3. Deterministic behavior

explaination.1. Adaptability: Incorrect! More characteristic of AI systems.
explaination.3. Deterministic behavior: Correct! Conventional systems execute fixed code deterministically.

question: An organization wants a system that can improve its fraud detection accuracy as new transactions become available. What AI characteristic supports this requirement?
options: 1. Transparency
2. Adaptability
3. Determinism
4. Static rules
answer: 2. Adaptability

explaination.2. Adaptability: Correct! Adaptability enables the system to update its knowledge and improve performance as new transactional data arrives.
explaination.4. Static rules: Incorrect! Static rules cannot adapt without manual rewriting.

question: Which statement best describes deterministic behavior?
options: 1. Outputs are based on probabilities.
2. Results vary each time the system runs.
3. The same input always produces the same output.

question: Which of the following is MOST likely an AI-based system?

question: Which type of AI includes all AI systems currently deployed in real-world applications?

explaination.1. General AI: Incorrect! General AI (AGI) does not yet exist in real-world deployments.
explaination.2. Super AI: Incorrect! Super AI is a hypothetical future category and is not currently deployed.
explaination.3. Narrow AI: Correct! All currently deployed real-world AI systems fall under Narrow AI (Weak AI), as they are designed to perform specific, bounded tasks.
explaination.4. Artificial Superintelligence: Incorrect! ASI is theoretical and far beyond current technology.

question: What distinguishes General AI from Narrow AI?
options: 1. It requires more training data.
2. It can only perform one task.
3. It can apply knowledge across multiple domains without task-specific retraining.
4. It always has internet access.

Incorrect! Training data volume does not define the architectural distinction of General AI.
Incorrect! Performing single or specialized tasks is characteristic of Narrow AI.
explaination.3. It can apply knowledge across multipl: Correct! General AI (AGI) is capable of human-like generalization, applying understanding and learning across diverse domains without requiring dedicated retraining for each new task.
Incorrect! Internet connectivity is unrelated to AI intelligence classifications.

question: Which statement about Frontier AI is correct?
options: 1. It is a form of Super AI.
2. It exceeds human intelligence.
3. It is the most advanced form of Narrow AI.
4. It possesses General Intelligence.
answer: 3. It is the most advanced form of Narrow AI.

Incorrect! Frontier AI refers to highly capable foundation models, which are still classified under Narrow AI.
Incorrect! They excel at specific tasks but do not possess general superhuman intelligence across all domains.
explaination.3. It is the most advanced form of Narro: Correct! Frontier AI represents state-of-the-art, highly versatile foundation models that remain within the broader category of Narrow AI.
Incorrect! They do not possess true General Intelligence (AGI).

question: According to the syllabus, which statement about General AI is true?
options: 1. Several General AI systems are already deployed.
2. General AI is synonymous with Frontier AI.
3. No AI system today possesses General Intelligence.

explaination.2. General AI is synonymous with Frontie: Incorrect! Frontier AI refers to advanced foundation models (still Narrow AI), whereas General AI is hypothetical.
explaination.3. No AI system today possesses General: Correct! According to standard AI testing and certification syllabi, true General Intelligence (AGI) has not yet been achieved.
explaination.4. General AI exceeds human intelligence: Incorrect! Exceeding human intelligence across all domains describes Super AI, while AGI matches human-level versatility.

question: What is meant by "technological singularity"?
options: 1. The point where AI loses internet access.
2. The transition from Narrow AI to General AI.
3. The transition from General AI to Super AI.
4. The replacement of machine learning by deep learning.
answer: 3. The transition from General AI to Super AI.

explaination.2. The transition from Narrow AI to Gene: Incorrect! This describes the achievement of AGI.
explaination.3. The transition from General AI to Sup: Correct! Technological singularity (or the intelligence explosion) refers to the hypothetical point where Super AI systems undergo recursive self-improvement, vastly and uncontrollably surpassing human intelligence.

question: Which AI category is characterized by continuous self-improvement without human intervention?
options: 1. Narrow AI
2. Frontier AI
3. General AI
4. Super AI
answer: 4. Super AI

explaination.1. Narrow AI: Incorrect! Narrow AI requires human retraining, curation, and intervention.
explaination.2. Frontier AI: Incorrect! Frontier AI models require human-driven updates and fine-tuning.
explaination.3. General AI: Incorrect! While AGI can learn, the specific concept of runaway recursive self-improvement without human limits defines Super AI.
explaination.4. Super AI: Correct! Super AI (Artificial Superintelligence) is theorized to possess recursive self-improvement capabilities, evolving autonomously beyond human control.

question: Which machine learning approach uses labeled data for training?
options: 1. Reinforcement Learning
2. Unsupervised Learning
3. Supervised Learning
4. Fuzzy Learning
answer: 3. Supervised Learning

explaination.1. Reinforcement Learning: Incorrect! Reinforcement learning relies on rewards and penalties from an environment, not labeled datasets.
explaination.2. Unsupervised Learning: Incorrect! Unsupervised learning works with unlabeled data to discover hidden patterns or clusters.
explaination.3. Supervised Learning: Correct! Supervised learning specifically trains algorithms using input features paired with ground-truth target labels.
explaination.4. Fuzzy Learning: Incorrect! Not a standard core machine learning training paradigm.

question: A machine learning model groups customers into similar segments without predefined labels. Which learning approach is being used?
options: 1. Supervised Learning
2. Reinforcement Learning
3. Deep Learning
4. Unsupervised Learning
answer: 4. Unsupervised Learning

explaination.3. Deep Learning: Incorrect! Deep learning can be supervised, unsupervised, or reinforcement-based; grouping without labels describes unsupervised learning.
explaination.4. Unsupervised Learning: Correct! Clustering algorithms group unlabeled data based on underlying similarities.

question: Which learning paradigm uses rewards and penalties to improve behavior?
options: 1. Supervised Learning
2. Reinforcement Learning
3. Unsupervised Learning
4. Bayesian Learning
answer: 2. Reinforcement Learning

explaination.2. Reinforcement Learning: Correct! Agents learn to make decisions by receiving rewards or penalties based on their actions in an environment.
explaination.3. Unsupervised Learning: Incorrect! Finds structures in unlabeled data.
explaination.4. Bayesian Learning: Incorrect! Based on probability and Bayes' theorem.

question: Which neural network architecture is most suitable for image recognition?
options: 1. Transformer
2. RNN
3. CNN
4. SVM

explaination.1. Transformer: Incorrect! Transformers are primarily designed for sequential data like text (though vision transformers exist, CNNs are the classic baseline).
explaination.2. RNN: Incorrect! RNNs are designed for sequential time-series or text data.
explaination.3. CNN: Correct! Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are specifically structured with spatial filters optimized for processing grid-like image data.
explaination.4. SVM: Incorrect! Support Vector Machines are traditional machine learning classifiers, not neural network architectures.

question: What is the relationship between AI, ML and DL?

explaination.3. AI contains ML which contains DL: Correct! Artificial Intelligence is the broad umbrella field, Machine Learning is a subset of AI, and Deep Learning is a specialized subset of Machine Learning using multi-layered neural networks.
explaination.4. ML contains AI which contains DL: Incorrect! AI encompasses ML, not the other way around.

question: Which technology is the primary foundation of modern large language models?
options: 1. Random Forest
2. Bayesian Models
3. Decision Trees
4. Transformers

explaination.1. Random Forest: Incorrect! An ensemble tree-based method, not the foundation of modern LLMs.
explaination.2. Bayesian Models: Incorrect! Statistical models used for probability estimation.
explaination.4. Transformers: Correct! The Transformer architecture (utilizing self-attention mechanisms) serves as the core foundation for modern large language models like GPT.

question: Which AI technology is primarily concerned with sentiment analysis and machine translation?
options: 1. NLP
2. Computer Vision
3. Fuzzy Logic
4. Random Forest

explaination.2. Computer Vision: Incorrect! Deals with images and video.
explaination.3. Fuzzy Logic: Incorrect! Handles reasoning with degrees of truth rather than true/false.
explaination.4. Random Forest: Incorrect! A machine learning algorithm, not a core technology domain like NLP.

question: What is a key characteristic of Agentic AI?
options: 1. It only classifies data.
2. It only generates text.
3. It plans, reasons and acts autonomously toward goals.
4. It replaces reinforcement learning.

Incorrect! Too narrow; agentic systems perform complex workflows.
Incorrect! They go beyond simple generation.
explaination.3. It plans, reasons and acts autonomous: Correct! Agentic AI systems possess autonomous capabilities to reason, break down multi-step plans, use tools, and execute actions to achieve specific objectives.
Incorrect! Agentic systems often leverage or build upon reinforcement learning principles.

question: Which technology uses two neural networks competing against each other to generate realistic synthetic data?
options: 1. Transformer
2. Diffusion Model
3. GAN
4. Random Forest
answer: 3. GAN

explaination.1. Transformer: Incorrect! Uses attention mechanisms for sequence modeling.
explaination.2. Diffusion Model: Incorrect! Generates data by iterative noise removal.
explaination.3. GAN: Correct! Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) consist of a generator and a discriminator network competing against each other to produce realistic synthetic data.

question: How do diffusion models generate high-quality content?
options: 1. By applying clustering algorithms
2. By adding and then removing noise from data
3. By using rule-based reasoning
4. By using reinforcement learning
answer: 2. By adding and then removing noise from data

explaination.1. By applying clustering algorithms: Incorrect! Clustering is for unsupervised grouping.
explaination.2. By adding and then removing noise fro: Correct! Diffusion models work by learning to iteratively denoise random Gaussian noise into structured, high-quality images or content.
explaination.3. By using rule-based reasoning: Incorrect! They are probabilistic deep generative models.
explaination.4. By using reinforcement learning: Incorrect! They are trained via diffusion processes, though RLHF can be applied later.

question: What mechanism is central to transformer models?
options: 1. Clustering
2. Gradient Boosting
3. Self-Attention
4. Decision Rules
answer: 3. Self-Attention

explaination.3. Self-Attention: Correct! The self-attention mechanism allows transformer models to weigh the importance of different words/tokens in a sequence regardless of their positional distance.

question: Which statement about Generative AI is TRUE?
options: 1. It is limited to classification tasks.
2. It can create new content such as text, images, and audio.
3. It only works with structured data.
4. It is based exclusively on reinforcement learning.
answer: 2. It can create new content such as text, images, and audio.

explaination.1. It is limited to classification tasks: Incorrect! Classification is predictive AI; GenAI creates new outputs.
explaination.2. It can create new content such as tex: Correct! Generative AI models are specifically designed to synthesize brand-new content across modalities like text, images, video, and audio.
Incorrect! It primarily operates on unstructured data (text, pixels, audio waveforms).
explaination.4. It is based exclusively on reinforcem: Incorrect! They are primarily trained on self-supervised pre-training followed by fine-tuning.

question: What is a foundation model typically used for?
options: 1. It is directly deployed without modification.
2. It is fine-tuned for specific applications.
3. It replaces all machine learning models.
4. It only supports image generation.
answer: 2. It is fine-tuned for specific applications.

explaination.1. It is directly deployed without modif: Incorrect! While zero-shot prompting is common, they are frequently adapted or fine-tuned.
explaination.2. It is fine-tuned for specific applica: Correct! Foundation models serve as broad, pre-trained base models that are subsequently fine-tuned or adapted for downstream domain-specific tasks.
explaination.3. It replaces all machine learning mode: Incorrect! They are not universal replacements for every specialized ML task.
Incorrect! They support text, multimodal inputs, code, and more.

question: Which concern is directly associated with the environmental impact of GenAI?
options: 1. Overfitting
2. Data Labeling
3. Carbon Footprint
4. Clustering Errors

explaination.1. Overfitting: Incorrect! A model generalization issue, not environmental.
explaination.2. Data Labeling: Incorrect! A data preparation cost/effort concern.
explaination.3. Carbon Footprint: Correct! Training and running massive generative AI foundation models consume immense electrical energy, resulting in a significant carbon footprint.
explaination.4. Clustering Errors: Incorrect! An unsupervised learning metric issue.

question: A model can process text, images, and audio as both inputs and outputs. According to the syllabus, this model is best described as:
options: 1. Supervised
2. Multimodal
3. Rule-Based
4. Bayesian
answer: 2. Multimodal

explaination.1. Supervised: Incorrect! Refers to training methodology with labels.
explaination.2. Multimodal: Correct! Multimodal AI models are capable of processing, integrating, and generating multiple data types or modalities (text, images, audio).

question: Which hardware characteristic is particularly beneficial for training machine learning models?
options: 1. High clock speed only
2. Massively parallel processing
3. Mechanical storage
4. Single-core execution
answer: 2. Massively parallel processing

explaination.1. High clock speed only: Incorrect! Single-core clock speed is less critical than parallelism for matrix math.
explaination.2. Massively parallel processing: Correct! Neural network training involves massive matrix multiplications that are efficiently accelerated through massively parallel processing architectures (like GPUs/TPUs).
explaination.3. Mechanical storage: Incorrect! Slow bottlenecks; modern training requires high-speed SSDs/RAM.
explaination.4. Single-core execution: Incorrect! Inefficient for deep learning workloads.

question: Why do GPUs generally outperform CPUs in machine learning applications?
options: 1. GPUs use less memory
2. GPUs have higher clock speeds
3. GPUs contain thousands of cores optimized for parallel processing
4. GPUs only support low-precision arithmetic
answer: 3. GPUs contain thousands of cores optimized for parallel processing

explaination.1. GPUs use less memory: Incorrect! GPUs often manage large VRAM pools.
explaination.2. GPUs have higher clock speeds: Incorrect! CPUs often have higher single-core clock speeds.
explaination.3. GPUs contain thousands of cores optim: Correct! GPUs feature thousands of smaller cores designed to execute parallel tensor and matrix operations simultaneously.
explaination.4. GPUs only support low-precision arith: Incorrect! They support high-precision float arithmetic as well.

question: What is the primary purpose of quantization in machine learning hardware?
options: 1. Increase model complexity
2. Improve network security
3. Reduce computational precision to improve efficiency
4. Increase training dataset size
answer: 3. Reduce computational precision to improve efficiency

explaination.3. Reduce computational precision to imp: Correct! Quantization converts weights from higher precision (e.g., FP32) to lower precision (e.g., INT8/INT4), reducing memory bandwidth requirements and accelerating inference speed.

question: According to the syllabus, AI-specific hardware such as ASICs is particularly suitable for:
options: 1. Spreadsheet processing
2. Edge computing
3. Database normalization
4. Manual software testing
answer: 2. Edge computing

explaination.1. Spreadsheet processing: Incorrect! Handled by standard general-purpose CPUs.
explaination.2. Edge computing: Correct! Application-Specific Integrated Circuits (ASICs) and specialized neural processing units provide high energy efficiency and performance required for deploying AI models on edge devices.

question: Which statement about training and inference is TRUE?
options: 1. They always require identical hardware.
2. Inference generally requires more computing power than training.
3. Training may be performed in the cloud, while inference can run on lower-end devices.
4. Inference can only be performed on GPUs.
answer: 3. Training may be performed in the cloud, while inference can run on lower-end devices.

explaination.1. They always require identical hardwar: Incorrect! Training demands heavy clusters, whereas inference can run on smartphones.
explaination.2. Inference generally requires more com: Incorrect! Training is computationally much more intensive.
explaination.3. Training may be performed in the clou: Correct! Training requires massive compute resources typically hosted in the cloud, whereas inference can often be optimized to run on lighter hardware or edge devices.

question: What distinguishes neuromorphic processors from traditional processors?
options: 1. They use higher clock frequencies.
2. They are based on brain-inspired architectures rather than the traditional von Neumann architecture.
3. They only support image processing.
4. They cannot be used for AI applications.

question: According to ISO/IEC 25059, which quality characteristic is defined as a new sub-characteristic of RELIABILITY that enables an AI-based system to maintain its level of functional correctness despite the presence of invalid inputs, adverse environmental conditions, or operator misuse?

question: What is a primary trade-off associated with using Application-Specific Integrated Circuits (ASICs) in AI deployments?

explaination.A. They combine biological nerve tissue: ASICs are entirely synthetic silicon chips and contain no biological tissue. Brain-inspired architectures that mimic biological neurons are Neuromorphic Processors.
explaination.C. They require continuous manual source: Hardware selection does not dictate manual code updates for weight adjustments; weights are updated through model retraining.
explaination.D. They convert deep neural networks int: ASICs execute ML tensor computations and do not convert neural networks into imperative rule-based expert systems.

question: A QA team is testing a speech-to-text AI model where ground-truth transcriptions are unavailable for noisy background audio. The team verifies that when background noise is reduced, output transcription accuracy must improve or remain equal, but never degrade. Which testing technique is being applied?
options: A. Back-to-Back Testing using a pseudo-oracle
B. Metamorphic Testing using a Monotonicity relation
C. Disparate Impact Analysis using counterfactual attributes
D. A/B Testing in production
answer: B. Metamorphic Testing using a Monotonicity relation

explaination.B. Metamorphic Testing using a Monotonic: Metamorphic Testing (MT) evaluates relational properties (Metamorphic Relations) between source and follow-up test cases when an exact test oracle is unavailable. Expecting accuracy to stay equal or improve (never degrade) upon input quality enhancement is a Monotonicity Metamorphic Relation.
explaination.A. Back-to-Back Testing using a pseudo-o: Back-to-Back testing compares SUT outputs directly against an independent reference implementation (pseudo-oracle).
explaination.C. Disparate Impact Analysis using count: Disparate Impact Analysis tests for fairness and bias by swapping sensitive demographic attributes.
explaination.D. A/B Testing in production: A/B testing compares live customer traffic across two operational model variants to evaluate business performance metrics.

question: A testing team evaluates an AI credit scoring system for potential gender bias. They create two identical applicant profiles, differing only by changing the gender attribute from male to female, and analyze whether prediction scores vary significantly. Which technique is being executed?
options: A. Disparate Impact Analysis using counterfactual attributes
B. Data Representativeness Testing using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
C. Model Conversion Testing using quantization
D. Black-box Adversarial Testing using surrogate models
answer: A. Disparate Impact Analysis using counterfactual attributes

explaination.A. Disparate Impact Analysis using count: Disparate Impact Analysis detects system bias by identifying sensitive attributes, generating counterfactual test cases (swapping sensitive values like gender or race while holding other variables constant), and evaluating output disparities.
explaination.B. Data Representativeness Testing using: Kolmogorov-Smirnov testing compares continuous feature distributions between sample datasets and operational profiles during representativeness testing.
explaination.C. Model Conversion Testing using quanti: Model conversion testing verifies accuracy retention and latency after converting models into target deployment formats (e.g., ONNX, 4-bit quantization).
explaination.D. Black-box Adversarial Testing using s: Black-box adversarial testing generates imperceptible input perturbations to trigger misclassifications.

question: A QA team needs to test an image classification model whose internal architecture and parameters are hidden (black-box access). Which property or technique should they leverage to craft effective adversarial test inputs?
options: A. Disparate Impact Analysis using counterfactual attributes
B. Transferability property using a white-box surrogate model
C. Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME)
D. Inter-Annotator Agreement using Cohen's Kappa
answer: B. Transferability property using a white-box surrogate model

explaination.B. Transferability property using a whit: The transferability property states that adversarial examples generated against a fully accessible white-box surrogate model often transfer successfully to fool an independent black-box target model trained on similar tasks.
explaination.A. Disparate Impact Analysis using count: Disparate Impact Analysis measures demographic fairness and bias, not adversarial robustness against image perturbations.
explaination.C. Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Ex: LIME provides local post-hoc explainability for black-box predictions; it does not generate adversarial test inputs.
explaination.D. Inter-Annotator Agreement using Cohen: Cohen's Kappa measures Inter-Annotator Agreement during label correctness testing.

question: A financial software company wants to test a newly updated fraud detection model against real-time live customer transactions. B. Shadow Testing
C. Rollback Testing

answer: B. Shadow Testing

explaination.B. Shadow Testing: Shadow testing routes live production requests to both the current and new models simultaneously in real time, but only returns the output of the current model to live users. This enables safe evaluation on live operational data with zero risk to users.
explaination.A. Canary Testing: Canary testing actively returns the new model's responses to a small subset (e.g., 5%) of live production users.
explaination.C. Rollback Testing: Rollback testing verifies recovery mechanisms to safely revert to a previous stable state if deployment fails.
explaination.D. Installability Testing: Installability testing verifies that software installs, configures, and uninstalls correctly across target hardware.

question: Which TWO statements regarding Machine Learning training datasets, validation datasets, and test datasets are TRUE?

answer: B. The validation dataset is used to evaluate model performance and tune hyperparameters.
C. The holdout test dataset must remain completely independent of training and hyperparameter tuning to provide an unbiased final evaluation.

explaination.B. The validation dataset is used to eva: Correct! In standard 3-way data splitting, the validation set is used for intermediate evaluation and hyperparameter tuning, while the independent holdout test set is reserved exclusively for unbiased final testing.

explaination.C. Transparency is classified under Inte: Correct! Under Product Quality, Transparency is a sub-characteristic of **Interaction Capability**; under Quality in Use, it is a sub-characteristic of **Satisfaction**.

question: A medical team implements Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) to provide clinicians with visual rationales for an AI lesion-detection system. Which trade-off is explicitly highlighted in the ISTQB CTAI syllabus regarding such Explainable AI (XAI) tools?
options: A. XAI tools convert deep learning models into locked, deterministic rule binaries.
B. The extra computational overhead required to generate explanations may compromise overall system performance.
C. XAI tools automatically remove non-determinism from GPU-based matrix operations.
D. XAI tools violate the EU AI Act compliance mandates for high-risk systems.
answer: B. The extra computational overhead required to generate explanations may compromise overall system performance.

explaination.A. XAI tools convert deep learning model: Inccorect! LIME is an external post-hoc explanation wrapper; it does not change or convert the underlying neural network into a rule binary
explaination.B. The extra computational overhead requ: Correct! The ISTQB CTAI syllabus (Section 2.1.2) explicitly states that while XAI tools like LIME provide insights into an AI system's decision-making process, they are computationally intensive and **may compromise system performance** (e.g., adding response latency).
explaination.C. XAI tools automatically remove non-de: Incorect! LIME does not alter hardware/GPU parallel execution or eliminate non-determinism.
explaination.D. XAI tools violate the EU AI Act compl: Incorect! The EU AI Act requires transparency and explainability for high-risk systems; XAI tools help fulfill regulatory expectations rather than violating them.

question: **Which TWO of the following factors make guaranteeing precise behavior inherently challenging in safety-related AI-based systems?** *(Select 2 options)*
options: A. Non-determinism caused by random seed initialization or minor input variations.
B. Static source code structure in conventional imperative programming.
C. Behavioral drift resulting from continuous post-deployment self-learning.
D. Standardized compliance with ISO 26262-6 in non-AI hardware components.
E. Mandatory 100% accuracy guarantees offered by deep learning frameworks.
answer: A. Non-determinism caused by random seed initialization or minor input variations.
C. Behavioral drift resulting from continuous post-deployment self-learning.

explaination.A. Non-determinism caused by random seed: Correct! Non-determinism (from floating-point precision, GPU parallelism, or random seeds) causes output variations for identical or slightly modified inputs.
explaination.B. Static source code structure in conve: Inccorect! Static source code pertains to conventional software, where behavior is predictable and deterministic.
explaination.C. Behavioral drift resulting from conti: Correct! Self-learning changes model parameters dynamically in live environments, moving the system away from its tested state.
explaination.D. Standardized compliance with ISO 2626: Inccorect! ISO 26262-6 compliance for non-AI components simplifies traditional safety verification; it is not an AI unpredictability factor.
explaination.E. Mandatory 100% accuracy guarantees of: Incorect! Deep learning models are probabilistic and can *never* guarantee 100% accuracy.

question: How do acceptance criteria for AI-based systems generally differ from those applied to conventional software systems?
options: A. AI acceptance criteria are always binary pass/fail statements based on rigid boolean logic.
B. AI acceptance criteria are purely qualitative and cannot be stated using numerical figures.
C. AI acceptance criteria are frequently statistical, probabilistic, or threshold-based due to inherent output variability.
D. AI acceptance criteria apply only to hardware power consumption rather than functional model outputs.
answer: C. AI acceptance criteria are frequently statistical, probabilistic, or threshold-based due to inherent output variability.

explaination.A. AI acceptance criteria are always bin: Inccorect! Binary pass/fail conditions work for deterministic conventional code, but fail to evaluate probabilistic AI performance fairly
explaination.B. AI acceptance criteria are purely qua: Inccorect! AI metrics are highly quantitative (e.g., Precision, F1-score, latency thresholds).
explaination.C. AI acceptance criteria are frequently: Correct! Because ML models produce probabilistic outputs rather than deterministic results, acceptance criteria must accommodate acceptable error margins using statistical metrics, probabilities, or threshold limits (e.g., Accuracy >=95%, Recall >=90%).
explaination.D. AI acceptance criteria apply only to: Inccorect! Acceptance criteria apply across all product quality and quality in use characteristics, not just hardware power usage.

question: Which THREE of the following are VALID examples of acceptance criteria for AI-specific quality characteristics specified in ISO/IEC 25059?
options: A. An image recognition model must achieve an accuracy of at least 95% on the test dataset.** *(AI functional correctness)
B. A power grid management system must provide a 30-second window during which an engineer can veto an AI-proposed critical action before execution.** *(Intervenability)

explaination.A. An image recognition model must achie: Correct! Accuracy >= 95% is a standard threshold-based criterion for AI functional correctness.

explaination.C. The deep learning framework must be c: Incorect! This specifies implementation details rather than a quality acceptance criterion.
explaination.D. An engine management system must adap: Correct! Adapting engine parameters within 20 seconds upon crossing altitude thresholds exemplifies **Functional adaptability** under Functional Suitability.
explaination.E. The neural network must guarantee 100: Inccorect! Expecting 100% zero-defect accuracy in probabilistic neural networks is mathematically impossible and invalid for AI systems

question: An e-commerce company develops an ML model that automatically groups users based on shared browsing behaviors without using historical category labels. Which form of machine learning is being utilized?
options: A. Supervised Learning – Classification
B. Unsupervised Learning – Clustering
C. Supervised Learning – ML Regression
D. Reinforcement Learning – Reward Hacking
answer: B. Unsupervised Learning – Clustering

explaination.A. Supervised Learning – Classification: Incorrect! Supervised classification requires labeled data to assign inputs to predefined discrete target classes.
explaination.B. Unsupervised Learning – Clustering: Correct! Unsupervised learning works with unlabeled data to uncover hidden structures, and clustering specifically groups data points based on feature similarity.
explaination.C. Supervised Learning – ML Regression: Incorrect! ML regression predicts continuous numerical values using labeled input-output pairs.
explaination.D. Reinforcement Learning – Reward Hacki: Incorrect! Reinforcement learning involves an agent interacting with an environment via trial and error, and reward hacking is an unintended optimization failure mode in RL.

question: During the Model Generation phase of the ML workflow, an ML engineer configures the maximum depth of a decision tree and the number of epochs for training. According to ISTQB CTAI terminology, how are these parameters classified?
options: A. Decision tree depth is an algorithm hyperparameter; epoch count is a model parameter.
B. Decision tree depth is a model hyperparameter; epoch count is an algorithm hyperparameter.
C. Both decision tree depth and epoch count are learned model weights.
D. Decision tree depth is a model parameter; epoch count is a model hyperparameter.
answer: B. Decision tree depth is a model hyperparameter; epoch count is an algorithm hyperparameter.

explaination.A. Decision tree depth is an algorithm h: Incorrect! Tree depth defines model structure (model hyperparameter), whereas model parameters are the internal weights/biases learned during training.
explaination.B. Decision tree depth is a model hyperp: Correct! Model hyperparameters set the structural properties of the model (e.g., tree depth, layer count), while algorithm hyperparameters control the training process execution (e.g., epoch count, learning rate).
explaination.C. Both decision tree depth and epoch co: Incorrect! Neither is learned automatically during training; both must be configured prior to training.
explaination.D. Decision tree depth is a model parame: Incorrect! Model parameters are learned dynamically by the algorithm (e.g., node weights), not manually configured.

question: An engineering team wants to enable a Large Language Model (LLM) to answer queries using an up-to-date internal company knowledge base without modifying the underlying neural network weights. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
options: A. Supervised Fine-Tuning
B. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
C. Quantization to 4-bit precision
D. Single-layer Perceptron training
answer: B. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

explaination.A. Supervised Fine-Tuning: Incorrect! Fine-tuning updates the internal model weights by training on domain-specific datasets.
explaination.B. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): Correct! RAG dynamically retrieves relevant external context from a database or document store to supplement queries without altering the pretrained model's internal weights.
explaination.C. Quantization to 4-bit precision: Incorrect! Quantization compresses model weight precision to reduce memory and compute overhead.
explaination.D. Single-layer Perceptron training: Incorrect! Training a single-layer perceptron creates a simple binary linear classifier and cannot update an LLM context pipeline.

question: Which set of activities represents core tasks performed during the Data Preparation phase of the ML workflow?
options: A. Data preprocessing, feature engineering, and exploratory data analysis (EDA).
B. Backpropagation, loss calculation, and weight optimization.
C. Red teaming, metamorphic relation derivation, and A/B testing.
D. Model card documentation, canary deployment, and shadow testing.
answer: A. Data preprocessing, feature engineering, and exploratory data analysis (EDA).

explaination.A. Data preprocessing, feature engineeri: Correct! Data preparation encompasses data cleaning/transformation/augmentation (preprocessing), feature selection/extraction (feature engineering), and distribution visualization (EDA).
explaination.B. Backpropagation, loss calculation, an: Incorrect! These activities occur during the Model Generation (training) phase.
explaination.C. Red teaming, metamorphic relation der: Incorrect! These are test techniques applied during Model Testing and Deployment Testing.
explaination.D. Model card documentation, canary depl: Incorrect! These activities belong to Model Documentation and Deployment Testing.

question: Why is it critical to keep the Test Dataset (Holdout set) strictly separate from the Training and Validation Datasets during ML model development?
options: A. To allow the model to learn noise patterns directly from the holdout dataset.
B. To ensure that final performance testing yields an unbiased assessment of the model's ability to generalize to unseen operational data.
C. To prevent algorithm hyperparameters from being updated during neural network forward passes.
D. To eliminate the need for k-fold cross-validation when training data is scarce.
answer: B. To ensure that final performance testing yields an unbiased assessment of the model's ability to generalize to unseen operational data.

explaination.A. To allow the model to learn noise pat: Incorrect! Models must never learn from or fit to the holdout test dataset.
explaination.B. To ensure that final performance test: Correct! The holdout test set must remain unexposed to training and hyperparameter tuning so it can evaluate true generalization performance without optimistic bias.
explaination.C. To prevent algorithm hyperparameters: Incorrect! Forward passes calculate output loss; hyperparameter updates do not occur during forward passes.
explaination.D. To eliminate the need for k-fold cros: Incorrect! Cross-validation is used on the training/validation pool specifically when data is scarce, but an independent holdout set is still required for unbiased final testing.

question: A data team is preparing a dataset for an AI model that predicts a rare industrial defect occurring in only 1% of manufacturing samples. When partitioning data for k-fold cross-validation, which technique MUST be applied to ensure every fold maintains this exact 1% defect proportion?
options: A. Pure Random Sampling
B. Stratified Sampling
C. Bootstrap Sampling with replacement
D. Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation
answer: B. Stratified Sampling

explaination.A. Pure Random Sampling: Incorrect! Random sampling in imbalanced datasets can produce folds with zero positive defect instances.
explaination.B. Stratified Sampling: Correct! Stratified sampling enforces that each split/fold retains the exact class distribution ratios present in the complete dataset.
explaination.C. Bootstrap Sampling with replacement: Incorrect! Bootstrap sampling generates random resamples with replacement, which does not guarantee proportional class representation across folds.
explaination.D. Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation: Incorrect! Leave-one-out splits data into N folds of 1 sample each, which cannot maintain class ratios per fold.

question:
An automated medical diagnosis model was evaluated on an independent holdout test dataset of 200 patient records. The resulting Confusion Matrix shows:

- False Positives (FP) = 10

answer: A. Accuracy = 85.0%, Precision = 87.5%, Recall = 77.8%, F1-score = 82.4%

explaination.B. Accuracy = 85.0%, Precision = 77.8%,: Incorrect! Precision and Recall values are swapped.

explaination.D. Accuracy = 90.0%, Precision = 70.0%,: Incorrect! Calculations for Accuracy, Precision, and Recall are incorrect.

question: A fraud detection system must ensure that missing a fraudulent transaction (False Negative) is minimized because it results in severe financial loss ($1,000,000+), while falsely flagging a legitimate transaction (False Positive) only causes a minor verification delay. Which metric should be PRIMARILY maximized?
options: A. Precision
B. Accuracy
C. Recall (Sensitivity)
D. k-Multisection Neuron Coverage
answer: C. Recall (Sensitivity)

explaination.A. Precision: Incorrect! Maximizing Precision minimizes False Positives, which would reduce customer delays at the expense of missing fraudulent transactions.
explaination.B. Accuracy: Incorrect! Accuracy treats False Positives and False Negatives equally, which is misleading when costs are highly asymmetric.
explaination.C. Recall (Sensitivity): Correct! Recall measures the proportion of actual positive fraud cases correctly flagged (TP / [TP + FN]). Maximizing Recall directly minimizes False Negatives.
explaination.D. k-Multisection Neuron Coverage: Incorrect! kMNC is a structural coverage metric for neural network testing, not a classification performance metric.

question: Which of the following statements regarding the basic architecture and training of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) is TRUE?
options: A. Node weights and biases are updated during the forward pass using activation functions.
B. Backpropagation calculates output loss and feeds error signals backward through the layers to adjust weights and biases.
C. An epoch refers to a single node calculation inside a hidden layer.
D. Deep neural networks consist strictly of an input layer and a single output node without hidden layers.
answer: B. Backpropagation calculates output loss and feeds error signals backward through the layers to adjust weights and biases.

explaination.A. Node weights and biases are updated d: Incorrect! The forward pass computes predictions; weight/bias updates occur during backpropagation.
explaination.B. Backpropagation calculates output los: Correct! Backpropagation propagates the error gradient backward through the network layers to update internal parameters (weights and biases).
explaination.C. An epoch refers to a single node calc: Incorrect! An epoch represents one complete pass of the entire training dataset through the neural network.
explaination.D. Deep neural networks consist strictly: Incorrect! Networks without hidden layers are single-layer perceptrons, whereas deep neural networks contain one or more hidden layers.

question: A single-layer Perceptron is best suited for solving which type of problem?
options: A. Linearly separable binary classification problems.
B. Complex multi-modal video sequence analysis.
C. Unsupervised spatial clustering of dense point clouds.
D. High-dimensional generative image diffusion.
answer: A. Linearly separable binary classification problems.

explaination.A. Linearly separable binary classificat: Correct! A Perceptron uses a single decision boundary (hyperplane) and can only solve linearly separable binary problems (e.g., AND/OR logic gates).
explaination.B. Complex multi-modal video sequence an: Incorrect! Sequence analysis requires deep recurrent or transformer architectures.
explaination.C. Unsupervised spatial clustering of de: Incorrect! Perceptrons are supervised models and cannot perform unsupervised clustering.
explaination.D. High-dimensional generative image dif: Incorrect! Generative image diffusion requires deep multi-layer convolutional or transformer networks.

question: A test team measures neural network coverage during dynamic testing. They calculate the proportion of neurons whose output values exceed the maximum value or fall below the minimum value observed during training. Which structural coverage metric is being evaluated?
options: A. Neuron Coverage
B. k-Multisection Neuron Coverage (kMNC)
C. Neuron Boundary Coverage (NBC)
D. Feature Selection Coverage
answer: C. Neuron Boundary Coverage (NBC)

explaination.A. Neuron Coverage: Incorrect! Neuron Coverage measures the proportion of neurons whose activation values exceed a fixed threshold.
explaination.B. k-Multisection Neuron Coverage (kMNC): Incorrect! kMNC divides the output range of each neuron into k equal sections and measures the proportion of sections covered.
explaination.C. Neuron Boundary Coverage (NBC): Correct! NBC evaluates whether test inputs push neuron outputs beyond their established training boundaries (exceeding maximum or falling below minimum training values).
explaination.D. Feature Selection Coverage: Incorrect! Feature selection is a data preparation activity, not a neural network structural coverage measure.

question:
A QA team evaluates an image classification model across three dataset splits and records the following F1-scores:
- Training Set F1-score: 99.2%
- Validation Set F1-score: 98.7%
- Independent Test Set (Holdout) F1-score: 58.4%

Which condition is occurring, and what is the MOST effective remediation strategy?
options: A. Underfitting; remediate by simplifying the model architecture and reducing training epochs.
B. Overfitting; remediate by collecting more diverse training data, applying data augmentation, or reducing model complexity.
C. Optimal fitting; deploy the model immediately because training performance exceeds 99%.
D. Reward Hacking; adjust the environment reward penalty function.
answer: B. Overfitting; remediate by collecting more diverse training data, applying data augmentation, or reducing model complexity.

explaination.A. Underfitting; remediate by simplifyin: Incorrect! Underfitting causes low performance across both training and validation sets.
explaination.B. Overfitting; remediate by collecting: Correct! High performance on training/validation datasets combined with a severe drop on an unseen test set indicates Overfitting. Effective fixes include data augmentation, gathering diverse data, or applying regularization/reducing model complexity.
explaination.C. Optimal fitting; deploy the model imm: Incorrect! High training score paired with 58.4% test score represents severe failure on unseen data.
explaination.D. Reward Hacking; adjust the environmen: Incorrect! Reward hacking is unique to Reinforcement Learning trial-and-error agents.

question: Which TWO statements accurately contrast Supervised Learning and Reinforcement Learning?
options: A. Supervised learning trains models on labeled input-output pairs, whereas reinforcement learning trains agents via trial-and-error environmental feedback.
B. Reinforcement learning relies on clustering unlabeled data points into spatial centroids.
C. Supervised learning algorithms adjust weights using rewards and penalties, whereas reinforcement learning uses backpropagation exclusively on holdout sets.
D. Reinforcement learning risks reward hacking when reward functions are poorly specified.
E. Both supervised learning and reinforcement learning require complete ground-truth labels for every input state prior to training.
answer: A. Supervised learning trains models on labeled input-output pairs, whereas reinforcement learning trains agents via trial-and-error environmental feedback.
D. Reinforcement learning risks reward hacking when reward functions are poorly specified.

explaination.A. Supervised learning trains models on: Correct! Supervised learning maps inputs to target labels, while RL agents learn optimal policies via environmental rewards and penalties.
explaination.B. Reinforcement learning relies on clus: Incorrect! Clustering unlabeled data is Unsupervised Learning.
explaination.C. Supervised learning algorithms adjust: Incorrect! Rewards and penalties belong to Reinforcement Learning, not Supervised Learning.
explaination.D. Reinforcement learning risks reward h: Correct! In RL, an agent may exploit loopholes in a flawed reward function to maximize its score without achieving the intended goal (reward hacking).
explaination.E. Both supervised learning and reinforc: Incorrect! Reinforcement learning does not use fixed ground-truth target labels; it learns dynamically from reward signals.

question: Which of the following statements correctly compares the testability of locked AI-based systems and adaptive AI-based systems?
options: A. Adaptive systems are easier to test post-deployment because their internal weights and biases remain permanently frozen.
B. Locked systems are easier to test post-deployment because their behavior remains static, whereas adaptive systems introduce test complexity as their behavior can change dynamically.
C. Locked systems exhibit continuous behavior drift during testing, requiring continuous real-time Blue Teaming monitoring.
D. Adaptive systems do not require pre-deployment testing because they learn exclusively in live production environments.
answer: B. Locked systems are easier to test post-deployment because their behavior remains static, whereas adaptive systems introduce test complexity as their behavior can change dynamically.

explaination.A. Adaptive systems are easier to test p: Incorrect! Locked AI-based systems have fixed weights and biases post-deployment, whereas adaptive systems continue to learn and evolve.
explaination.B. Locked systems are easier to test pos: Correct! Locked AI-based systems have fixed behavior post-deployment, making them mostly deterministic and easier to test, while adaptive systems introduce complexity because their behavior can change during or after testing.
explaination.C. Locked systems exhibit continuous beh: Incorrect! Adaptive systems (not locked systems) suffer from behavior drift over time as they learn from new operational data.
explaination.D. Adaptive systems do not require pre-d: Incorrect! Adaptive systems can and must be rigorously tested before deployment (e.g., simulating changes in environmental conditions or testing the learning mechanism itself).

question: Why is a statistical approach required when testing probabilistic AI-based systems?
options: A. Because a single test failure (e.g., misclassifying one cat) cannot accurately reflect the overall functional correctness of a probabilistic model.
