B. Because statistical testing eliminates the need to reserve an independent holdout test dataset.
C. Because conventional deterministic pass/fail criteria function identically for deep neural networks and imperative source code.
D. Because statistical testing allows development teams to bypass regulatory safety thresholds.
answer: A. Because a single test failure (e.g., misclassifying one cat) cannot accurately reflect the overall functional correctness of a probabilistic model.

explaination.A. Because a single test failure (e.g.,: Correct! AI-based systems are fundamentally probabilistic and non-deterministic, so a single test instance cannot reflect overall correctness; test suites must be sufficiently large to yield statistically significant results across data distributions.
explaination.B. Because statistical testing eliminate: Incorrect! Statistical testing relies directly on representative holdout test datasets to evaluate model performance distributions.
explaination.C. Because conventional deterministic pa: Incorrect! Deterministic pass/fail per individual test case is insufficient for probabilistic AI models.
explaination.D. Because statistical testing allows de: Incorrect! Regulatory frameworks in healthcare or transport actually mandate statistical testing to demonstrate compliance with safety and fairness thresholds.

question: A test team faces the test oracle problem when evaluating a complex AI model that lacks an exact ground-truth answer for new inputs. Which technique provides a pseudo-oracle by comparing the System Under Test against an independent alternative reference implementation?
options: A. Red Teaming
B. Back-to-Back Testing
C. Metamorphic Testing
D. Exploratory Testing
answer: B. Back-to-Back Testing

explaination.A. Red Teaming: Incorrect! Red Teaming is a proactive, pre-deployment fault attack probing GenAI/AI systems for harmful outputs.
explaination.B. Back-to-Back Testing: Correct! Back-to-back testing uses an alternative version of the system as a reference point (a pseudo-oracle) and compares its outputs with those of the system under test when presented with the same inputs.
explaination.C. Metamorphic Testing: Incorrect! Metamorphic testing verifies relational properties (metamorphic relations) between source and follow-up test cases rather than using an independent reference system as a pseudo-oracle.
explaination.D. Exploratory Testing: Incorrect! Exploratory testing is an informal, experience-based test design technique.

question: Which of the following test approaches addresses the test oracle problem by training a secondary model on labeled data to predict expected outcomes for unlabeled test cases?
options: A. Metamorphic Testing
B. Environmental Boundary Definition
C. Proxy Oracles
D. Blue Teaming
answer: C. Proxy Oracles

explaination.A. Metamorphic Testing: Incorrect! Metamorphic testing relies on metamorphic relations between related test cases rather than secondary predictive models.
explaination.B. Environmental Boundary Definition: Incorrect! Environmental boundary definition sets constraints on environmental conditions (e.g., lighting, temperature) to make outputs predictable.
explaination.C. Proxy Oracles: Correct! Proxy oracles use secondary systems or models (including other AI systems) trained on labeled data to assess or validate outputs when direct expected results are unavailable.
explaination.D. Blue Teaming: Incorrect! Blue Teaming consists of real-time defensive monitoring and input/output filtering in operational environments.

question: Which combination of factors primarily contributes to the 'Input Explosion Problem' when designing test cases for Generative AI applications?
options: A. Frozen neural network weights, 4-bit quantization, and single-turn system prompts.
B. System and user prompts, context window history, and tunable generation hyperparameters like Temperature and Max Tokens.
C. Confusion matrix dimensions, F1-score targets, and stratified k-fold splits.
D. Single-value range constraints, multi-value count limits, and Cohen's Kappa score metrics.
answer: B. System and user prompts, context window history, and tunable generation hyperparameters like Temperature and Max Tokens.

explaination.A. Frozen neural network weights, 4-bit: Incorrect! Frozen weights and quantization relate to model compilation and locking, not input space explosion.
explaination.B. System and user prompts, context wind: Correct! In Generative AI testing, the huge variety of system/user prompts, conversational context window lengths, and generation hyperparameters (e.g., Temperature, Max Tokens) leads to a massive, combinatorial input space known as the input explosion problem.
explaination.C. Confusion matrix dimensions, F1-score: Incorrect! These are metrics and splitting strategies for traditional supervised machine learning evaluation.
explaination.D. Single-value range constraints, multi: Incorrect! These relate to dataset constraints and inter-annotator agreement in input data testing.

question: What is a primary operational distinction between Red Teaming and Blue Teaming in AI system testing?
options: A. Red Teaming is a proactive pre-deployment attack activity, whereas Blue Teaming involves ongoing real-time defensive monitoring and filtering during operation.
B. Red Teaming tests conventional non-AI database code, whereas Blue Teaming tests deep learning neural network hyperparameters.
C. Red Teaming is an automated real-time production filter, whereas Blue Teaming is an informal unit test conducted during development.
D. Red Teaming applies exclusively to locked AI systems, whereas Blue Teaming applies exclusively to static rule-based systems.
answer: A. Red Teaming is a proactive pre-deployment attack activity, whereas Blue Teaming involves ongoing real-time defensive monitoring and filtering during operation.

explaination.A. Red Teaming is a proactive pre-deploy: Correct! Red Teaming proactively probes an AI system before deployment to discover harmful capabilities, while Blue Teaming provides ongoing real-time defensive monitoring and filtering of inputs/outputs in operational environments.
explaination.B. Red Teaming tests conventional non-AI: Incorrect! Red Teaming specifically targets AI models/systems to elicit policy-violating or harmful outputs.
explaination.C. Red Teaming is an automated real-time: Incorrect! The definitions are reversed; Blue Teaming performs real-time operational filtering.
explaination.D. Red Teaming applies exclusively to lo: Incorrect! Red Teaming is especially critical for Generative AI and adaptive systems.

question: A test lead is planning a Red Teaming assessment for a newly fine-tuned Generative AI chatbot before its commercial release. Which operational workflow represents an effective Red Teaming implementation?
options: A. Executing a single-turn prompt asking for public capital cities and marking the test passed if no crash occurs.

B. Engaging in multi-turn interactive dialogues (15–20 turns) using diverse personas and adversarial prompts to deliberately induce policy-violating outputs, then analyzing identified failure threats.
C. Running static code analysis on the data pre-processing pipeline to verify SQL parameter escaping.
D. Deploying the model directly to all end-users and reviewing customer complaint logs after 30 days.
answer: B. Engaging in multi-turn interactive dialogues (15–20 turns) using diverse personas and adversarial prompts to deliberately induce policy-violating outputs, then analyzing identified failure threats.

explaination.A. Executing a single-turn prompt asking: Incorrect! Single-turn factual prompts do not probe system guardrails or elicit complex harmful capabilities.
explaination.B. Engaging in multi-turn interactive di: Correct! Red Teaming for GenAI involves assembling diverse testers to engage in multi-turn interactive prompting (typically 15-20 turns) to uncover policy violations (e.g., hate speech, CBRN guidance), analyzing threats, and feeding data back for mitigations.
explaination.C. Running static code analysis on the d: Incorrect! Static code analysis is a conventional component test technique, not Red Teaming for GenAI safety.
explaination.D. Deploying the model directly to all e: Incorrect! Red Teaming is most effective when conducted before deployment in a safe test environment, rather than exposing live end-users to unverified risks.

question: During an exploratory testing exercise, a tester evaluates an LLM tasked with generating test cases using 2-value Boundary Value Analysis (BVA) for an integer input field with valid range [1]. The LLM generates the test set {0, 1, 100, 101}. How should the tester evaluate this output during session debrief?
options: A. Fail; the output is incorrect because 2-value BVA requires testing only two values overall: {1, 100}.
B. Pass; the output is correct and complete because 2-value BVA evaluates the boundary value and its immediate neighbor outside the boundary for both minimum and maximum limits.
C. Fail; the output is incorrect because {0, 1, 100, 101} represents 3-value BVA.
D. Pass; 2-value BVA requires testing six values: {0, 1, 2, 99, 100, 101}.
answer: B. Pass; the output is correct and complete because 2-value BVA evaluates the boundary value and its immediate neighbor outside the boundary for both minimum and maximum limits.

explaination.A. Fail; the output is incorrect because: Incorrect! Testing only {1, 100} evaluates boundary values without immediate invalid neighbors.
explaination.B. Pass; the output is correct and compl: Correct! In 2-value BVA, each boundary (min = 1, max = 100) requires testing two values: the boundary itself and its adjacent outside value (min: 1 and 0; max: 100 and 101), yielding the complete set {0, 1, 100, 101}.
explaination.C. Fail; the output is incorrect because: Incorrect! 3-value BVA would include boundary values, inside neighbors, and outside neighbors: {0, 1, 2, 99, 100, 101}.
explaination.D. Pass; 2-value BVA requires testing si: Incorrect! Testing six values describes 3-value BVA, not 2-value BVA.

question: According to the ISTQB CTAI syllabus, which two specialized test levels are specifically designed to address Machine Learning risks?
options: A. Unit Testing and System Integration Testing
B. Input Data Testing and ML Model Testing
C. Component Testing and User Acceptance Testing
D. API Testing and Performance Efficiency Testing
answer: B. Input Data Testing and ML Model Testing

explaination.A. Unit Testing and System Integration T: Incorrect! These are conventional software test levels.
explaination.B. Input Data Testing and ML Model Testi: Correct! The ISTQB CTAI syllabus explicitly defines two specialized test levels to address unique machine learning risks: Input Data Testing (Chapter 5) and ML Model Testing (Chapter 6).
explaination.C. Component Testing and User Acceptance: Incorrect! These are conventional software test levels.
explaination.D. API Testing and Performance Efficienc: Incorrect! API testing and performance testing are conventional integration/non-functional test types.

question: A software engineering team is developing a machine learning application. How should conventional test levels (e.g., Component Testing, Component Integration Testing) be applied alongside specialized ML test levels?
options: A. Conventional test levels are entirely replaced by ML Model Testing and cannot be used for MLS.
B. Conventional test levels are used to test non-AI components, pipeline integration, and host application embedding, while specialized ML test levels address unique ML risks.
C. Conventional test levels are applied exclusively to trained neural network weights and biases.
D. Conventional test levels are executed only during post-deployment Blue Teaming.
answer: B. Conventional test levels are used to test non-AI components, pipeline integration, and host application embedding, while specialized ML test levels address unique ML risks.

explaination.A. Conventional test levels are entirely: Incorrect! Conventional test levels remain fully relevant for non-AI code and overall system integration.
explaination.B. Conventional test levels are used to: Correct! Non-AI components (UI, databases, preprocessors) and API integrations are tested using conventional test levels, while specialized ML test levels (Input Data Testing and ML Model Testing) handle ML-specific risks.
explaination.C. Conventional test levels are applied: Incorrect! Neural network weights and biases are evaluated under specialized ML Model Testing.
explaination.D. Conventional test levels are executed: Incorrect! Conventional test levels span the entire development lifecycle before deployment.

question: When applying Risk-Based Testing to a Machine Learning System, how are risks uniquely categorized compared to non-AI software?
options: A. Risks are categorized strictly by C++ compiler warning levels.
B. Risks are categorized across Input Data risks, ML Model risks, and Quality Characteristics risks defined in ISO/IEC 25059.
C. Risks are limited exclusively to physical hardware GPU overheating.
D. Risks are categorized based solely on the number of lines of Python code in the repository.
answer: B. Risks are categorized across Input Data risks, ML Model risks, and Quality Characteristics risks defined in ISO/IEC 25059.

explaination.A. Risks are categorized strictly by C++: Incorrect! Compiler warnings do not reflect AI/ML functional, data, or model risks.
explaination.B. Risks are categorized across Input Da: Correct! Risk-based testing for ML systems categorizes risks into Input Data risks (e.g., data bias, unrepresentative data), ML Model risks (e.g., overfitting, adversarial vulnerabilities), and ISO/IEC 25059 quality characteristic risks.
explaination.C. Risks are limited exclusively to phys: Incorrect! Hardware overheating is a general infrastructure risk, not an ML software quality risk taxonomy.
explaination.D. Risks are categorized based solely on: Incorrect! Lines of code do not determine ML risk profiles.

question: A bank is integrating a 3rd-party credit scoring ML service via a REST API (AIaaS). The primary risk identified during risk analysis is that mismatched JSON data schemas between the bank's core application and the external service could cause transaction dropouts. Which test level should be prioritized to mitigate this specific risk?
options: A. Input Data Testing focused on label correctness in third-party training data.
B. Component Integration Testing focused on API testing and data exchange schema validation.
C. Metamorphic testing focused on neuron boundary coverage.
D. Red Teaming focused on multi-turn CBRN prompt injection.
answer: B. Component Integration Testing focused on API testing and data exchange schema validation.

explaination.A. Input Data Testing focused on label c: Incorrect! Label correctness testing evaluates training labels, which does not test schema compatibility over API integrations.
explaination.B. Component Integration Testing focused: Correct! When integrating AI components or third-party AIaaS services via APIs, Component Integration Testing (specifically API testing) validates interface data exchange, schema compatibility, and error handling.
explaination.C. Metamorphic testing focused on neuron: Incorrect! Metamorphic testing and neuron boundary coverage evaluate model internal behavior, not API integration schemas.
explaination.D. Red Teaming focused on multi-turn CBR: Incorrect! CBRN prompt injection is a GenAI safety attack, irrelevant to REST API JSON schema integration.

question: Which of the following are appropriate approaches to testing the input data of a machine learning system? (Choose TWO answers.)
options: A. Reviewing the data to identify potential quality issues.
B. Performing exploratory data analysis to discover patterns and anomalies.
C. Assuming that data collected from production is always correct.
D. Testing only the model's source code because input data quality is not part of testing.
E. Replacing all input data with synthetic data without checking whether it represents real-world conditions.
answer: A. Reviewing the data to identify potential quality issues.
B. Performing exploratory data analysis to discover patterns and anomalies.

explaination.A. Reviewing the data to identify potent: Correct! Data reviews can identify defects, inconsistencies, missing values, and other potential quality problems before the data is used by the machine learning system.
explaination.B. Performing exploratory data analysis: Correct! Exploratory data analysis (EDA) helps testers understand distributions, identify unusual observations, discover patterns, and investigate potential data quality problems.
explaination.C. Assuming that data collected from pro: Incorrect! Production data can contain missing values, invalid records, bias, unexpected distributions, and other defects. Its origin does not guarantee its quality.
explaination.D. Testing only the model's source code: Incorrect! Input data testing is an important part of testing machine learning systems. Data defects can lead to incorrect predictions even when the model implementation is technically correct.
explaination.E. Replacing all input data with synthet: Incorrect! Synthetic data can be useful, but it must be assessed for quality and representativeness. Replacing real data indiscriminately may introduce additional problems.

question: A machine learning team obtains training data from an external supplier. The supplier cannot explain where the data originated, how it was collected, or how it was modified. Which testing approach is MOST directly relevant to investigating this risk?
options: A. Data provenance testing.
B. Dataset constraint testing only.
C. Neuron coverage testing.
D. Label correctness testing only.
answer: A. Data provenance testing.

Correct! Data provenance testing investigates the origin, history, ownership, collection, and transformations of data. It is particularly relevant when data comes from untrustworthy sources or is poorly managed.
Incorrect! Constraint testing checks whether records satisfy predefined rules, such as valid types and ranges. It does not, by itself, establish where the data originated or whether its source is trustworthy.
Incorrect! Neuron coverage is a structural coverage measure used when testing neural networks. It does not directly investigate the origin or history of training data.
Incorrect! Label correctness testing checks whether assigned labels are accurate and consistent. Correct labels do not establish that the data source is trustworthy.

question: Which statements about input data risks and their mitigations are CORRECT? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. Incorrect data types and out-of-range values can be investigated using dataset constraint testing.
B. Missing data and insufficient coverage of target classes can be investigated using data representativeness testing.
C. Incorrect or inconsistent labels can be investigated using label correctness testing.
D. Poorly managed data can be considered safe if the model achieves high accuracy.
E. Feature selection problems can always be solved by increasing the size of the training dataset.
answer: A. Incorrect data types and out-of-range values can be investigated using dataset constraint testing.
B. Missing data and insufficient coverage of target classes can be investigated using data representativeness testing.
C. Incorrect or inconsistent labels can be investigated using label correctness testing.

explaination.A. Incorrect data types and out-of-range: Correct! Dataset constraint testing checks whether the dataset conforms to predefined requirements, including permitted data types, value ranges, and consistency rules.
explaination.B. Missing data and insufficient coverag: Correct! Data representativeness testing helps identify gaps in the dataset, including missing information, inadequate class coverage, and insufficient representation of relevant use cases.
explaination.C. Incorrect or inconsistent labels can: Correct! Label correctness testing investigates whether the labels accurately and consistently describe the associated data.
explaination.D. Poorly managed data can be considered: Incorrect! High overall accuracy does not establish data provenance, integrity, fairness, or security. A model can perform well on a particular dataset while still having serious data quality problems.
explaination.E. Feature selection problems can always: Incorrect! Increasing the dataset size does not necessarily improve feature selection. Feature testing and feature engineering are more directly relevant to determining whether selected features are informative and appropriate.

question: A recruitment model is trained on historical hiring data. The historical dataset contains substantially fewer successful applicants from one gender because of past discriminatory hiring practices. Which statements are CORRECT? (Choose TWO answers.)
options: A. Historical skews in the training data can be a source of bias.
B. A model trained on historical decisions is necessarily fair because the decisions were made by humans.
C. Testing for bias should consider whether the system treats people differently based on sensitive attributes.
D. High overall classification accuracy proves that the model does not discriminate.
E. Removing all records associated with the underrepresented gender is an appropriate general solution.
answer: A. Historical skews in the training data can be a source of bias.
C. Testing for bias should consider whether the system treats people differently based on sensitive attributes.

explaination.A. Historical skews in the training data: Correct! Historical data can encode previous discriminatory practices. A model may learn and reproduce these patterns unless the risks are identified and addressed.
explaination.B. A model trained on historical decisio: Incorrect! Human decisions can themselves contain bias. Learning from historical decisions does not guarantee fair outcomes.
explaination.C. Testing for bias should consider whet: Correct! Bias testing investigates potentially unfair differences associated with sensitive attributes such as gender, age, or race.
explaination.D. High overall classification accuracy: Incorrect! Overall accuracy does not establish fairness across demographic groups. Group-specific metrics and appropriate fairness analyses may reveal disparities hidden by aggregate performance.
explaination.E. Removing all records associated with: Incorrect! Removing an entire group can worsen representativeness and fairness. Appropriate mitigation requires investigating the source of bias and selecting a justified intervention.

question: Which of the following are potential sources of bias in a machine learning system? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. Unrepresentative training data.
B. Historical skews in the data.
C. Problems in the algorithm, model, or ML development framework that introduce systemic unfairness.
D. The existence of a validation dataset.
E. Using an appropriate data type for a numerical feature.
answer: A. Unrepresentative training data.
B. Historical skews in the data.
C. Problems in the algorithm, model, or ML development framework that introduce systemic unfairness.

Correct! If training data does not adequately represent the relevant population or use cases, the resulting model may perform differently across groups or situations.
Correct! Existing inequalities or imbalances in historical data can be learned by the model and reproduced in its predictions.
explaination.C. Problems in the algorithm, model, or: Correct! Bias is not exclusively a data problem. The algorithm, model design, or development framework can also contribute to unfair outcomes.
explaination.D. The existence of a validation dataset: Incorrect! A validation dataset is a normal part of model development. Its existence is not inherently a source of bias, although its quality and representativeness matter.
explaination.E. Using an appropriate data type for a: Incorrect! Using the correct data type is a data quality practice. It does not inherently introduce bias, although inappropriate representation or preprocessing could cause problems.

question: A lender wants to investigate whether changing an applicant's gender, while keeping other relevant characteristics unchanged, affects the loan model's prediction. Which testing approach is MOST directly relevant?
options: A. Disparate impact analysis using counterfactual examples.
B. Dataset constraint testing of numerical ranges only.
C. Data pipeline performance testing.
D. Neuron coverage testing.
answer: A. Disparate impact analysis using counterfactual examples.

explaination.A. Disparate impact analysis using count: Correct! The approach can involve identifying sensitive attributes, generating counterfactuals that change those attributes, obtaining model outputs, and comparing the results for potentially unfair differences.
explaination.B. Dataset constraint testing of numeric: Incorrect! Checking numerical ranges can identify invalid data but does not directly investigate whether a sensitive attribute affects model decisions.
Incorrect! Pipeline performance testing investigates operational characteristics such as throughput and latency. It does not directly assess disparate treatment based on gender.
Incorrect! Neuron coverage measures how many neurons are activated beyond a specified threshold during testing. It does not directly establish whether the model treats applicants fairly.

question: Which statements about data pipeline testing are CORRECT? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. Component testing can examine data ingestion components and transformation scripts.
B. Data pipeline testing can investigate whether data quality defects compromise pipeline outputs.
C. Operational data pipelines may require testing for reliability, performance, and maintainability.
D. Data pipeline testing is unnecessary if individual model tests pass.
E. Data pipeline testing is limited to checking whether the pipeline produces output without errors.
answer: A. Component testing can examine data ingestion components and transformation scripts.
B. Data pipeline testing can investigate whether data quality defects compromise pipeline outputs.
C. Operational data pipelines may require testing for reliability, performance, and maintainability.

explaination.A. Component testing can examine data in: Correct! Pipeline component testing can examine individual elements such as data ingestion, transformation logic, and sensor interfaces.
explaination.B. Data pipeline testing can investigate: Correct! Pipeline testing checks whether data is handled and transformed correctly and whether defects affect the resulting data.
explaination.C. Operational data pipelines may requir: Correct! Operational pipelines must support dependable, efficient, and maintainable processing. Their testing priorities differ from those of exploratory training pipelines.
explaination.D. Data pipeline testing is unnecessary: Incorrect! A model may pass tests when supplied with prepared test data while the production pipeline still introduces errors, drops records, or transforms features incorrectly.
explaination.E. Data pipeline testing is limited to c: Incorrect! Producing output does not guarantee that the output is correct, complete, secure, or timely. Pipeline testing must address more than successful execution.

question: A production data pipeline transforms customer records before passing them to a machine learning model. The transformation code runs without exceptions, but the pipeline silently converts some monetary amounts from one currency to another without applying the correct exchange rate. What is the MOST appropriate conclusion?
options: A. The pipeline is correct because it executes without exceptions.
B. The pipeline has a data transformation defect that can compromise output data quality.
C. The issue can only be detected by testing the model's neural network coverage.
D. The issue is exclusively a label correctness problem.
answer: B. The pipeline has a data transformation defect that can compromise output data quality.

explaination.A. The pipeline is correct because it ex: Incorrect! Successful execution does not prove semantic correctness. A pipeline can run successfully while producing incorrect values.
explaination.B. The pipeline has a data transformatio: Correct! The transformation applies incorrect business logic, so the resulting data is wrong even though the pipeline completes execution.
explaination.C. The issue can only be detected by tes: Incorrect! Neural network coverage is not the appropriate primary technique. Testing the transformation logic and verifying the pipeline's outputs can directly reveal the defect.
explaination.D. The issue is exclusively a label corr: Incorrect! The defect affects a numerical feature transformation, not necessarily the label assigned to an example. It is primarily a pipeline and data integrity problem.

question: Which statements about data representativeness are CORRECT? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. The training dataset should adequately cover relevant target classes and use cases.
B. A dataset containing a very large number of records is automatically representative.
C. Data distributions and feature ranges should be considered when assessing representativeness.
D. Missing data and insufficient coverage can be indicators of representativeness problems.
E. Data augmentation always improves representativeness regardless of the generated samples.
answer: A. The training dataset should adequately cover relevant target classes and use cases.
C. Data distributions and feature ranges should be considered when assessing representativeness.
D. Missing data and insufficient coverage can be indicators of representativeness problems.

explaination.A. The training dataset should adequatel: Correct! The dataset should reflect the range of relevant situations the model is expected to handle. Insufficient class or use-case coverage can lead to poor generalization.
explaination.B. A dataset containing a very large num: Incorrect! Dataset size alone does not guarantee representativeness. A large dataset can still systematically exclude important populations, classes, or operating conditions.
explaination.C. Data distributions and feature ranges: Correct! Understanding the distributions and ranges of relevant features helps identify whether the dataset adequately reflects expected operational conditions.
explaination.D. Missing data and insufficient coverag: Correct! Missing information and inadequate coverage can leave important parts of the intended population or use cases underrepresented.
explaination.E. Data augmentation always improves rep: Incorrect! Augmentation can introduce skew or unrealistic samples. Its effect on representativeness depends on how the additional data is generated and whether it reflects relevant real-world conditions.

question: A company trains an image classification model using photographs captured almost exclusively in bright daylight. After deployment, the model performs poorly on photographs captured at night. Which testing activity would MOST directly help investigate this problem before deployment?
options: A. Testing data representativeness by checking coverage of relevant lighting conditions.
B. Checking whether all image filenames use the same naming convention.
C. Measuring neuron coverage without examining the training data.
D. Verifying only that the training pipeline completes successfully.
answer: A. Testing data representativeness by checking coverage of relevant lighting conditions.

explaination.A. Testing data representativeness by ch: Correct! Night-time conditions are part of the expected operational environment. Assessing whether the dataset represents these conditions can reveal a coverage gap before deployment.
explaination.B. Checking whether all image filenames: Incorrect! Filename consistency may be useful for data management, but it does not directly address the lack of night-time images.
explaination.C. Measuring neuron coverage without exa: Incorrect! Neuron coverage may provide information about which neurons activate during testing, but it does not directly establish whether the dataset represents different lighting conditions.
explaination.D. Verifying only that the training pipe: Incorrect! Successful execution does not establish data representativeness or generalization to conditions missing from the training data.

question: A dataset contains customer ages that must be integers between 18 and 100 inclusive. Which of the following records violate the age constraint? (Choose TWO answers.)
options: A. Age = 18
B. Age = 45
C. Age = 101
D. Age = 17
E. Age = 100
answer: C. Age = 101
D. Age = 17

explaination.A. Age = 18: Incorrect as a violation. The value is valid because the lower boundary of 18 is inclusive.
explaination.B. Age = 45: Incorrect as a violation. The value is an integer within the permitted range.
explaination.C. Age = 101: Correct! The value exceeds the maximum permitted age of 100 and violates the range constraint.
explaination.D. Age = 17: Correct! The value is below the minimum permitted age of 18 and violates the range constraint.
explaination.E. Age = 100: Incorrect as a violation. The value is valid because the upper boundary of 100 is inclusive.

question: A machine learning dataset has the following constraints: customer_id must be unique, age must be an integer between 18 and 100 inclusive, income must be non-negative, and loan_status must be either APPROVED or REJECTED. Which records violate at least one constraint? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. customer_id = 1001, age = 25, income = 50000, loan_status = APPROVED
B. customer_id = 1002, age = 17, income = 30000, loan_status = REJECTED
C. customer_id = 1003, age = 40, income = -500, loan_status = APPROVED
D. customer_id = 1004, age = 35, income = 60000, loan_status = PENDING
E. customer_id = 1001, age = 30, income = 40000, loan_status = REJECTED
answer: B. customer_id = 1002, age = 17, income = 30000, loan_status = REJECTED
C. customer_id = 1003, age = 40, income = -500, loan_status = APPROVED
D. customer_id = 1004, age = 35, income = 60000, loan_status = PENDING

explaination.A. customer_id = 1001, age = 25, income: Incorrect as a violation. The age is within range, income is non-negative, and loan_status is an allowed value. Assuming this is the first occurrence of customer_id 1001, the record satisfies the constraints.
explaination.B. customer_id = 1002, age = 17, income: Correct! The age of 17 is below the permitted minimum of 18.
explaination.C. customer_id = 1003, age = 40, income: Correct! The income is negative, violating the non-negative income constraint.
explaination.D. customer_id = 1004, age = 35, income: Correct! PENDING is not one of the permitted loan_status values, which are APPROVED and REJECTED.
explaination.E. customer_id = 1001, age = 30, income: Correct! This record duplicates customer_id 1001 from option A, violating the uniqueness constraint. Note that this means the question has FOUR violating records, not THREE.

question: A tester needs to verify that a dataset's transaction_date field contains valid dates, that transaction_amount is numeric, and that transaction_id is unique. Which testing approach is MOST appropriate?
options: A. Dataset constraint testing.
B. Disparate impact analysis.
C. Label correctness testing.
D. Data representativeness testing only.
answer: A. Dataset constraint testing.

Correct! Dataset constraint testing verifies compliance with predefined rules, including data types, valid values, required fields, and uniqueness constraints.
Incorrect! Disparate impact analysis investigates potentially unfair differences associated with sensitive attributes. It does not directly validate field types or unique identifiers.
Incorrect! Label correctness testing checks whether assigned labels are accurate and consistent. The stated requirements concern general dataset integrity.
Incorrect! Representativeness testing investigates whether the dataset adequately covers the intended population and relevant conditions. It is not the primary method for checking data types and identifier uniqueness.

question: Why is label correctness testing important for supervised machine learning? (Choose TWO answers.)
options: A. Incorrect labels can cause a model to learn incorrect associations between input attributes and outcomes.
B. Inaccurate or inconsistent labels can undermine model performance and generalization.
C. Correct labels guarantee that the model will never overfit.
D. Label correctness testing eliminates the need for representative training data.
E. Label correctness testing proves that the model's architecture is optimal.
answer: A. Incorrect labels can cause a model to learn incorrect associations between input attributes and outcomes.
B. Inaccurate or inconsistent labels can undermine model performance and generalization.

explaination.A. Incorrect labels can cause a model to: Correct! In supervised learning, labels provide the target outcomes used during training. Incorrect labels can teach the model misleading relationships.
explaination.B. Inaccurate or inconsistent labels can: Correct! Label quality directly affects the learning process. Incorrect or inconsistent labels can reduce the model's ability to make reliable predictions on unseen data.
explaination.C. Correct labels guarantee that the mod: Incorrect! Even with correct labels, a model can overfit by learning patterns that do not generalize well to new data.
explaination.D. Label correctness testing eliminates: Incorrect! Correct labels do not compensate for missing classes, unrepresentative samples, or insufficient coverage of relevant operating conditions.
explaination.E. Label correctness testing proves that: Incorrect! Label correctness testing evaluates the quality of the target labels, not whether the model architecture is optimal.

question: A medical image dataset contains images labeled BENIGN or MALIGNANT. Which approaches can be used to investigate whether the labels are correct? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. Ask qualified medical experts to review a sample of labeled images.
B. Have multiple qualified annotators independently label the same images and compare their agreement.
C. Check the labeling guidelines for ambiguity and inconsistency.
D. Assume that every label is correct because it was entered by a trained annotator.
E. Measure the data pipeline's throughput and treat high throughput as evidence that the labels are correct.
answer: A. Ask qualified medical experts to review a sample of labeled images.
B. Have multiple qualified annotators independently label the same images and compare their agreement.
C. Check the labeling guidelines for ambiguity and inconsistency.

explaination.A. Ask qualified medical experts to revi: Correct! Expert review can identify inaccurate labels by comparing annotations with domain knowledge and appropriate labeling criteria.
explaination.B. Have multiple qualified annotators in: Correct! Multiple annotation can reveal disagreements and help assess annotation consistency. Disagreements may require adjudication or clarification of the guidelines.
explaination.C. Check the labeling guidelines for amb: Correct! Ambiguous or inconsistent labeling rules can cause systematic annotation errors. Reviewing and improving the guidelines helps address the underlying problem.
explaination.D. Assume that every label is correct be: Incorrect! Trained annotators can still make mistakes, misunderstand guidelines, or disagree about ambiguous cases. Training does not guarantee correctness.
explaination.E. Measure the data pipeline's throughpu: Incorrect! Throughput measures processing performance, not semantic label accuracy. A pipeline can process incorrect labels quickly.

question: Two annotators independently label the same set of images. They disagree on 30% of the images, especially those containing ambiguous visual features. What is the MOST appropriate next step?
options: A. Assume the first annotator is always correct.
B. Investigate the disagreements, review the labeling guidelines, and use qualified review or adjudication where appropriate.
C. Delete every image on which the annotators disagree without further investigation.
D. Conclude that the model is overfitting because the annotators disagree.
answer: B. Investigate the disagreements, review the labeling guidelines, and use qualified review or adjudication where appropriate.

explaination.A. Assume the first annotator is always: Incorrect! There is no basis for assuming that the first annotator is more accurate. Disagreements should be investigated using appropriate evidence and labeling rules.
explaination.B. Investigate the disagreements, review: Correct! High disagreement can indicate ambiguous cases, unclear guidelines, or annotation errors. Investigating disagreements helps improve label quality and consistency.
explaination.C. Delete every image on which the annot: Incorrect! Removing disputed examples indiscriminately can reduce dataset size and representativeness and may eliminate difficult but important cases.
explaination.D. Conclude that the model is overfittin: Incorrect! Annotator disagreement is evidence of a potential label quality or ambiguity problem, not proof of model overfitting. Overfitting concerns the model's ability to generalize beyond its training data.

question: Which statements about the relationship between input data testing and model quality are CORRECT? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. High-quality input data is important for reliable machine learning behavior.
B. A model can learn misleading associations from incorrect training labels.
C. Input data quality problems can remain even when the model implementation contains no coding defects.
D. Passing all dataset constraint tests proves that the model is fair and generalizes well.
E. Testing the input data removes the need to test the trained model.
answer: A. High-quality input data is important for reliable machine learning behavior.
B. A model can learn misleading associations from incorrect training labels.
C. Input data quality problems can remain even when the model implementation contains no coding defects.

explaination.A. High-quality input data is important: Correct! Machine learning systems depend on data for training and prediction. Data quality problems can compromise model behavior.
explaination.B. A model can learn misleading associat: Correct! Incorrect labels can cause the model to associate input features with incorrect target outcomes.
explaination.C. Input data quality problems can remai: Correct! A technically correct implementation can still learn from biased, incomplete, inconsistent, or incorrectly labeled data.
explaination.D. Passing all dataset constraint tests: Incorrect! Constraint testing checks predefined data rules. It does not establish fairness, representativeness, or generalization.
explaination.E. Testing the input data removes the ne: Incorrect! Input data testing and model testing address different risks. Both are necessary to obtain appropriate evidence about the quality of a machine learning system.

question: A company uses data augmentation to increase the number of training images. After augmentation, the dataset contains many more images of one target class than the others, and several generated images are unrealistic. Which statements are CORRECT? (Choose TWO answers.)
options: A. Data augmentation can introduce skew into a dataset.
B. A larger dataset is always more representative than a smaller dataset.
C. Data representativeness testing can help investigate class imbalance and coverage.
D. Synthetic or augmented data never requires quality assessment.
E. The problem can only be resolved by increasing the number of neural network layers.
answer: A. Data augmentation can introduce skew into a dataset.
C. Data representativeness testing can help investigate class imbalance and coverage.

explaination.A. Data augmentation can introduce skew: Correct! Augmentation can change class proportions or create unrealistic patterns. Its impact on dataset quality should be assessed rather than assumed to be beneficial.
explaination.B. A larger dataset is always more repre: Incorrect! A larger dataset may contain more duplicated, biased, unrealistic, or irrelevant samples. Size alone does not guarantee representativeness.
explaination.C. Data representativeness testing can h: Correct! This testing can reveal whether the dataset adequately represents target classes and relevant use cases.
explaination.D. Synthetic or augmented data never req: Incorrect! Generated data can introduce defects, distort distributions, or fail to reflect real-world conditions. It should be assessed for its intended purpose.
explaination.E. The problem can only be resolved by i: Incorrect! Adding layers does not correct an unrepresentative dataset. The data generation and preparation process should be investigated.

question: Which of the following correctly matches a machine learning model risk with an appropriate testing approach? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. A model produces unfair predictions for different demographic groups — testing for bias.
B. A model performs well on training data but poorly on unseen data — testing for overfitting.
C. A model's input data distribution changes after deployment — drift testing.
D. A model has an API defect — metamorphic testing only.
E. A model produces harmful or undesirable outputs — dataset constraint testing only.
answer: A. A model produces unfair predictions for different demographic groups — testing for bias.
B. A model performs well on training data but poorly on unseen data — testing for overfitting.
C. A model's input data distribution changes after deployment — drift testing.

explaination.A. A model produces unfair predictions f: Correct! Testing for bias investigates whether the model produces potentially unfair outcomes, including differences associated with sensitive attributes.
explaination.B. A model performs well on training dat: Correct! Overfitting occurs when a model learns the training data too specifically and fails to generalize adequately to unseen examples.
explaination.C. A model's input data distribution cha: Correct! Drift testing monitors changes in operational data and the relationships between inputs and expected outcomes.
explaination.D. A model has an API defect — metamorph: Incorrect! API testing is the direct approach for detecting API defects. Metamorphic testing addresses functional relationships between related inputs and outputs, especially when expected outputs are difficult to determine.
explaination.E. A model produces harmful or undesirab: Incorrect! Exploratory testing and red teaming are relevant approaches for investigating harmful outputs. Dataset constraints alone cannot establish that a model's generated outputs are safe or appropriate.

question: A model update introduces a defect that causes an existing prediction service to return incorrect results for previously supported inputs. Which testing approaches are MOST appropriate for detecting these problems? (Choose TWO answers.)
options: A. Exploratory testing of the updated model.
B. Regression testing to check whether previously working behavior has been affected.
C. Dataset representativeness testing only.
D. Label correctness testing only.
E. Data provenance testing only.
answer: A. Exploratory testing of the updated model.
B. Regression testing to check whether previously working behavior has been affected.

explaination.A. Exploratory testing of the updated mo: Correct! Exploratory testing can help discover unexpected behaviors and defects introduced by the model update.
explaination.B. Regression testing to check whether p: Correct! Regression testing checks whether changes have caused previously working functionality to fail or behave incorrectly.
explaination.C. Dataset representativeness testing on: Incorrect! Representativeness testing investigates whether data adequately reflects the intended population and operating conditions. It does not directly establish whether an update has broken existing functionality.
Incorrect! Label correctness testing examines the accuracy and consistency of labels. It is not sufficient to detect every defect introduced by a model update.
Incorrect! Data provenance testing examines data origin and history. It does not directly test the updated model's behavior against previously supported inputs.

question: Why is reviewing machine learning model documentation important? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. It helps identify missing, inaccurate, or inconsistent information about the model.
B. It helps testers understand the model's intended purpose, limitations, and evaluation results.
C. It helps determine whether sufficient information is available to support testing, deployment, and maintenance.
D. It guarantees that the model's predictions are correct.
E. It eliminates the need for testing the model because documentation is sufficient evidence of quality.
answer: A. It helps identify missing, inaccurate, or inconsistent information about the model.
B. It helps testers understand the model's intended purpose, limitations, and evaluation results.
C. It helps determine whether sufficient information is available to support testing, deployment, and maintenance.

explaination.A. It helps identify missing, inaccurate: Correct! Documentation reviews assess the completeness, accuracy, consistency, clarity, and usefulness of the information provided about the model.
explaination.B. It helps testers understand the model: Correct! Documentation should help stakeholders understand what the model is intended to do, how it was evaluated, and what limitations or risks are known.
explaination.C. It helps determine whether sufficient: Correct! Documentation provides information needed for test planning, evaluation, operational monitoring, maintenance, and informed deployment decisions.
explaination.D. It guarantees that the model's predic: Incorrect! Documentation describes the model and provides evidence about its evaluation, but reviewing the documentation cannot guarantee correct predictions.
explaination.E. It eliminates the need for testing th: Incorrect! Documentation review complements, rather than replaces, model testing. Claims and reported results may need to be verified through independent testing.

question: Which information would be relevant when reviewing machine learning model documentation? (Choose FOUR answers.)
options: A. The model's intended purpose, intended users, and known limitations.
B. The datasets used for training, validation, and testing, including their characteristics and sources.
C. The model's evaluation metrics and the acceptance criteria used to assess its performance.
D. Operational monitoring metrics, alerts, and the strategy for updating or rolling back the model.
E. Only the name of the model's developer, because other details are unnecessary for testing.
answer: A. The model's intended purpose, intended users, and known limitations.
B. The datasets used for training, validation, and testing, including their characteristics and sources.
C. The model's evaluation metrics and the acceptance criteria used to assess its performance.
D. Operational monitoring metrics, alerts, and the strategy for updating or rolling back the model.

explaination.A. The model's intended purpose, intende: Correct! These details establish the context in which the model should be evaluated and help identify inappropriate uses or unsupported assumptions.
explaination.B. The datasets used for training, valid: Correct! Dataset documentation helps reviewers assess data suitability, provenance, representativeness, and the independence of evaluation datasets.
explaination.C. The model's evaluation metrics and th: Correct! Reviewers need to understand how the model was evaluated and what criteria determine whether its performance is acceptable.
explaination.D. Operational monitoring metrics, alert: Correct! Operational documentation supports ongoing monitoring and helps teams respond to performance degradation or problematic model updates.
explaination.E. Only the name of the model's develope: Incorrect! Identifying the developer may be useful, but it is not sufficient. Testing requires information about the model's purpose, design, data, evaluation, limitations, and operational behavior.

question: A probabilistic machine learning classifier is required to achieve at least 95% accuracy. Which approach is MOST appropriate for evaluating whether it meets this requirement?
options: A. Execute one test case and accept the model if the prediction is correct.
B. Evaluate the model using a sufficiently large, representative, independent test dataset and compare the statistical results with predefined acceptance criteria.
C. Evaluate the model using only the training dataset because it contains the examples used to create the model.
D. Accept the model if its developer reports that it performed well during training.
answer: B. Evaluate the model using a sufficiently large, representative, independent test dataset and compare the statistical results with predefined acceptance criteria.

explaination.A. Execute one test case and accept the: Incorrect! A single correct prediction does not provide sufficient evidence that a probabilistic model meets a population-level accuracy requirement.
explaination.B. Evaluate the model using a sufficient: Correct! ML functional performance testing uses an independent and representative test dataset to measure performance and determine whether the statistical acceptance criteria are satisfied.
explaination.C. Evaluate the model using only the tra: Incorrect! Training data is not an appropriate substitute for an independent test dataset. Performance on training data may be optimistic, particularly when the model is overfitted.
explaination.D. Accept the model if its developer rep: Incorrect! A developer's report does not replace independent evaluation against defined acceptance criteria.

question: A test requirement states: 'The model must achieve 98% accuracy with a margin of error of ±4% at a 95% confidence level.' Which statements are CORRECT? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. The acceptance criterion includes both a performance target and statistical uncertainty requirements.
B. Increasing the sample size can improve the precision of the estimated performance.
C. The results should be interpreted in relation to the specified confidence level and margin of error.
D. A single successful prediction proves that the model meets the requirement.
E. The training dataset can replace the independent test dataset because the required accuracy is explicitly stated.
answer: A. The acceptance criterion includes both a performance target and statistical uncertainty requirements.
B. Increasing the sample size can improve the precision of the estimated performance.
C. The results should be interpreted in relation to the specified confidence level and margin of error.

explaination.A. The acceptance criterion includes bot: Correct! The requirement specifies a target accuracy and also constrains the uncertainty of the estimated accuracy through a margin of error and confidence level.
explaination.B. Increasing the sample size can improv: Correct! With the confidence level fixed, increasing the sample size generally reduces the margin of error, making the estimate more precise.
explaination.C. The results should be interpreted in: Correct! Statistical acceptance criteria require interpretation of the measured performance and its uncertainty rather than treating every result as a simple pass or fail without context.
explaination.D. A single successful prediction proves: Incorrect! One prediction provides insufficient statistical evidence to establish that the model achieves the specified accuracy.
explaination.E. The training dataset can replace the: Incorrect! A performance requirement does not remove the need for an independent test dataset. The test data should also represent the intended operational input domain.

question: Which statements correctly describe adversarial testing of machine learning systems? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. It investigates whether deliberately crafted inputs can cause incorrect or undesirable model behavior.
B. Adversarial examples may involve small changes to inputs that cause a model to make an incorrect prediction.
C. It can be performed manually or with automated algorithms that generate input variations.
D. It is exclusively concerned with checking whether the model's API returns a valid HTTP status code.
E. It can only be performed when the tester has complete access to the model's internal architecture and parameters.
answer: A. It investigates whether deliberately crafted inputs can cause incorrect or undesirable model behavior.
B. Adversarial examples may involve small changes to inputs that cause a model to make an incorrect prediction.
C. It can be performed manually or with automated algorithms that generate input variations.

explaination.A. It investigates whether deliberately: Correct! Adversarial testing deliberately probes weaknesses by constructing inputs designed to expose vulnerabilities in the model's behavior.
explaination.B. Adversarial examples may involve smal: Correct! An adversarial example may be created by modifying an input so that the model produces an incorrect or undesirable result, sometimes despite the change being difficult for a human to notice.
explaination.C. It can be performed manually or with: Correct! Testers may construct adversarial examples manually or use automated techniques to generate many candidate inputs.
explaination.D. It is exclusively concerned with chec: Incorrect! API response validation is a different testing concern. Adversarial testing focuses on model vulnerabilities exposed by deliberately crafted inputs.
explaination.E. It can only be performed when the tes: Incorrect! Adversarial testing can use black-box approaches that rely on observed inputs and outputs. White-box access can make certain attacks easier to construct but is not always required.

question: A face recognition model incorrectly identifies people when small, carefully designed changes are made to input images. Which testing approach is MOST directly relevant to investigating this weakness?
options: A. Adversarial testing.
B. Dataset constraint testing of image file extensions only.
C. Documentation review only.
D. A/B testing of two website layouts.
answer: A. Adversarial testing.

Correct! Adversarial testing investigates whether deliberately crafted inputs, including carefully modified images, can exploit weaknesses in a machine learning model.
explaination.B. Dataset constraint testing of image f: Incorrect! Checking image file extensions may identify input format problems but does not directly investigate susceptibility to adversarial image modifications.
Incorrect! Documentation review may identify known limitations or risks, but executing adversarial tests is more directly relevant to investigating the observed weakness.
Incorrect! Comparing website layouts does not address adversarial vulnerabilities in face recognition.

question: A tester is evaluating an image recognition model, but it is impractical to determine the correct output for every possible image. The tester wants to generate follow-up test cases from a previously passed test case. Which testing technique is MOST appropriate?
options: A. Metamorphic testing.
B. Dataset provenance testing.
C. Smoke testing only.
D. Usability testing.
answer: A. Metamorphic testing.

Correct! Metamorphic testing derives follow-up test cases from source test cases using a metamorphic relation. It is particularly useful when reliable expected outputs are difficult or expensive to obtain.
Incorrect! Data provenance testing investigates the origin and history of data rather than relationships between model outputs for related inputs.
Incorrect! Smoke testing checks whether essential functionality works after a build or deployment. It does not specifically derive follow-up cases using input-output relationships.
Incorrect! Usability testing evaluates how easily users can interact with a system. It does not directly address the test oracle problem described.

question: A route optimization model recommends a route between two locations. A tester creates a follow-up test by reversing the origin and destination. The tester expects the resulting route to connect the reversed endpoints but does not assume that the route must be identical. Which statement BEST describes this approach?
options: A. It uses a metamorphic relation that defines an expected relationship between the source and follow-up test results.
B. It proves that the model must return exactly the same route in both directions.
C. It is back-to-back testing because two model implementations are compared.
D. It is A/B testing because two different routes are displayed.
answer: A. It uses a metamorphic relation that defines an expected relationship between the source and follow-up test results.

explaination.A. It uses a metamorphic relation that d: Correct! A metamorphic relation specifies how an expected result should relate to the result of a modified input. Here, the route should connect the reversed endpoints, while the precise route may legitimately differ.
explaination.B. It proves that the model must return: Incorrect! Reversing the endpoints does not generally imply that the same route will be returned in reverse order. One-way streets, traffic, and route optimization criteria can change the result.
explaination.C. It is back-to-back testing because tw: Incorrect! Back-to-back testing compares the outputs of two or more implementations or versions for the same or equivalent inputs. The scenario describes deriving a follow-up input using a metamorphic relation.
explaination.D. It is A/B testing because two differe: Incorrect! A/B testing compares alternative versions or variants under an appropriate experimental setup. Merely obtaining two route results does not constitute A/B testing.

question: A sentiment analysis model classifies a customer review as NEGATIVE. The tester then changes the customer's name in the review while leaving the review's sentiment-bearing content unchanged. The tester expects the sentiment classification to remain unchanged. Which option BEST describes the test?
options: A. A metamorphic test using an invariance relation.
B. An adversarial test that necessarily requires a malicious attack.
C. A drift test measuring changes in operational data over months.
D. A back-to-back test comparing two different models.
answer: A. A metamorphic test using an invariance relation.

explaination.A. A metamorphic test using an invarianc: Correct! The tester changes an input property that should not affect sentiment and checks whether the output remains stable. This is an invariance relation. The validity of the test depends on the name change not altering the sentiment-bearing meaning.
explaination.B. An adversarial test that necessarily: Incorrect! The scenario does not require a malicious attack. Metamorphic testing can investigate ordinary functional consistency without attempting to exploit a vulnerability.
explaination.C. A drift test measuring changes in ope: Incorrect! Drift testing monitors changes over time in operational data distributions or relationships between inputs and outcomes. The scenario compares related inputs in a test.
explaination.D. A back-to-back test comparing two dif: Incorrect! No two implementations are being compared. The tester checks the relationship between outputs from two related inputs.

question: Which statements about metamorphic testing are CORRECT? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. A metamorphic relation describes how a change in input should affect the expected result.
B. Follow-up test cases can be derived from a previously passed source test case.
C. It is useful when a reliable test oracle is unavailable or expensive to use.
D. Every metamorphic relation must require the source and follow-up outputs to be identical.
E. Metamorphic testing guarantees correctness even when no source test case has passed.
answer: A. A metamorphic relation describes how a change in input should affect the expected result.
B. Follow-up test cases can be derived from a previously passed source test case.
C. It is useful when a reliable test oracle is unavailable or expensive to use.

explaination.A. A metamorphic relation describes how: Correct! A metamorphic relation defines the expected relationship between the source test's result and the follow-up test's result after the input is transformed.
explaination.B. Follow-up test cases can be derived f: Correct! A key feature of metamorphic testing is generating follow-up cases from source cases using defined transformations and relations.
explaination.C. It is useful when a reliable test ora: Correct! Metamorphic testing is particularly useful when the exact expected result cannot easily be determined for every input.
explaination.D. Every metamorphic relation must requi: Incorrect! Some relations require invariance, where outputs remain the same. Others require a predictable change, such as a directional change in the output.
explaination.E. Metamorphic testing guarantees correc: Incorrect! Metamorphic testing does not guarantee correctness. The reliability of its conclusions depends on the validity of the relations and the test cases. A previously passed source case provides a useful basis for deriving follow-up cases.

question: A deployed model receives customer transactions. Over several months, the distribution of transaction amounts and customer ages changes substantially compared with the training data. Which type of drift does this MOST directly indicate?
options: A. Data drift.
B. Concept drift.
C. Overfitting.
D. Reward hacking.
answer: A. Data drift.

Correct! Data drift occurs when the statistical properties or distribution of operational input data change over time relative to the reference data.
Incorrect! Concept drift refers to changes in the relationship between inputs and the target outcome. A change in input distributions alone most directly indicates data drift.
Incorrect! Overfitting occurs when a model learns the training data too specifically and generalizes poorly to unseen data. It does not describe the observed temporal change in input distributions.
Incorrect! Reward hacking occurs when a model exploits weaknesses in a reward or objective definition rather than achieving the intended goal. It is unrelated to the stated distribution change.

question: A fraud detection model continues to receive customer transactions with approximately the same feature distributions as before. However, fraudsters change their behavior, so the relationship between transaction characteristics and the actual occurrence of fraud changes. Which type of drift is MOST directly indicated?
options: A. Concept drift.
B. Data drift only.
C. Dataset constraint violation.
D. Label format drift.
answer: A. Concept drift.

Correct! Concept drift occurs when the relationship between the input features and the target outcome changes over time. Changing fraud patterns can make previously learned relationships less reliable.
Incorrect! Data drift concerns changes in the statistical properties of the input data. The scenario specifically states that feature distributions remain approximately stable while the relationship with the target changes.
Incorrect! A constraint violation occurs when data fails predefined rules. The scenario describes a changing relationship between inputs and outcomes, not invalid records.
Incorrect! The scenario does not describe a change in label representation or format. It describes a change in the meaning or predictive relationship of the input features.

question: Which activities are appropriate when testing an operational machine learning system for drift? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. Monitor operational input distributions and compare them with appropriate reference data.
B. Investigate changes in model performance and the relationship between inputs and target outcomes.
C. Define appropriate thresholds or conditions for triggering investigation or retraining.
D. Assume that the model will remain valid indefinitely once it passes its initial acceptance tests.
E. Retrain the model automatically after every small input change without assessing its significance.
answer: A. Monitor operational input distributions and compare them with appropriate reference data.
B. Investigate changes in model performance and the relationship between inputs and target outcomes.
C. Define appropriate thresholds or conditions for triggering investigation or retraining.

explaination.A. Monitor operational input distributio: Correct! Monitoring distributions helps identify data drift and can provide an early warning that operational inputs differ from the data used during development.
explaination.B. Investigate changes in model performa: Correct! Changes in performance and input-outcome relationships can indicate concept drift or other operational problems.
explaination.C. Define appropriate thresholds or cond: Correct! Monitoring needs actionable criteria so that significant changes can trigger investigation, corrective action, or retraining when justified.
explaination.D. Assume that the model will remain val: Incorrect! Operational environments and user behavior can change. Passing initial tests does not guarantee continued performance.
explaination.E. Retrain the model automatically after: Incorrect! Not every change is significant or harmful. Retraining should be based on suitable evidence and a controlled process; otherwise, unnecessary retraining can introduce new defects.

question: A classification model achieves 99% accuracy on its training dataset but only 72% accuracy on an independent test dataset. Which conclusion is MOST appropriate?
options: A. The model is likely overfitted.
B. The model is necessarily underfitted.
C. The model is proven to be fair.
D. The model has no generalization problem because its training accuracy is high.
answer: A. The model is likely overfitted.

Correct! A large gap between high training performance and substantially lower performance on unseen data is a typical indication of overfitting.
Incorrect! Underfitting generally occurs when a model fails to learn the relevant patterns adequately, often resulting in poor performance on both training and unseen data. The stated pattern more strongly suggests overfitting.
Incorrect! Accuracy differences between training and test datasets do not establish fairness. Fairness requires appropriate evaluation of potential unfair outcomes.
explaination.D. The model has no generalization probl: Incorrect! High training accuracy alone does not demonstrate good generalization. The substantially lower test accuracy indicates that generalization is a concern.

question: A model achieves low accuracy on both its training dataset and an independent test dataset. Which conclusion is MOST appropriate?
options: A. The model may be underfitted.
B. The model is necessarily overfitted.
C. The model is guaranteed to perform well after deployment.
D. The model has proven that the training dataset is representative.
answer: A. The model may be underfitted.

Correct! Poor performance on both training and test data can indicate that the model has not learned the relevant patterns adequately. Other causes, such as poor data quality or an inappropriate evaluation setup, should also be investigated.
Incorrect! Overfitting is typically indicated by strong training performance combined with weaker unseen-data performance. Poor performance on both datasets is more consistent with underfitting, although further investigation is necessary.
explaination.C. The model is guaranteed to perform we: Incorrect! Poor performance on both datasets provides no basis for guaranteeing good operational behavior.
explaination.D. The model has proven that the trainin: Incorrect! Model accuracy does not by itself prove representativeness. Data representativeness must be assessed using appropriate evidence about the target population and operating conditions.

question: A company wants to compare a new machine learning model with its existing production model to determine whether the new model improves a predefined business or performance metric. Which testing approach is MOST appropriate?
options: A. A/B testing.
B. Dataset constraint testing.
C. Label correctness testing.
D. Data provenance testing.
answer: A. A/B testing.

Correct! A/B testing compares two variants, such as an existing model and a new model, using appropriate metrics and statistical analysis to determine whether the observed difference supports an improvement.
Incorrect! Constraint testing checks whether data satisfies predefined rules. It does not directly compare the performance of two model variants.
Incorrect! Label correctness testing investigates whether target labels are accurate and consistent. It does not directly evaluate the comparative performance of two models.
Incorrect! Provenance testing investigates data origin and history. It does not directly measure whether the new model outperforms the existing model.

question: Which statements correctly describe A/B testing in the context of machine learning systems? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. It compares two variants using predefined performance or business metrics.
B. It can use statistical methods to assess whether observed differences are meaningful.
C. It can help determine whether a new model improves performance compared with an existing model.
D. It guarantees that the new model will be better in every operational situation.
E. It is the same as testing whether two implementations produce identical outputs for the same inputs.
answer: A. It compares two variants using predefined performance or business metrics.
B. It can use statistical methods to assess whether observed differences are meaningful.
C. It can help determine whether a new model improves performance compared with an existing model.

explaination.A. It compares two variants using predef: Correct! A/B testing compares variants using selected metrics, such as conversion rate, accuracy, or another relevant outcome.
explaination.B. It can use statistical methods to ass: Correct! Statistical analysis helps determine whether an observed difference is likely to reflect a real effect rather than random variation.
explaination.C. It can help determine whether a new m: Correct! A/B testing can provide evidence about whether a new model improves predefined outcomes relative to an existing model.
explaination.D. It guarantees that the new model will: Incorrect! A/B testing provides evidence about the measured outcomes under the tested conditions. It cannot guarantee superiority in every possible situation.
explaination.E. It is the same as testing whether two: Incorrect! That description is more closely associated with back-to-back testing. A/B testing evaluates comparative outcomes, which may differ between the variants.

question: A team has two implementations of the same machine learning algorithm. The team supplies the same test inputs to both implementations and compares their outputs to identify unexpected differences. Which testing approach is MOST appropriate?
options: A. Back-to-back testing.
B. A/B testing exclusively.
C. Drift testing.
D. Label correctness testing.
answer: A. Back-to-back testing.

Correct! Back-to-back testing compares the outputs of two or more implementations or versions for the same or equivalent inputs. Differences can reveal defects or unexpected behavior.
Incorrect! A/B testing compares variants using selected metrics and an appropriate experimental approach. Directly comparing outputs from implementations supplied with the same inputs is characteristic of back-to-back testing.
Incorrect! Drift testing investigates changes in operational input distributions or input-outcome relationships over time.
Incorrect! Label correctness testing checks the accuracy and consistency of labels, not differences between the outputs of two model implementations.

question: A machine learning team replaces a model library with a new implementation. Both implementations are expected to behave equivalently for the same inputs, but there is no affordable way to determine the correct output for every possible input. Which approach is MOST appropriate for identifying unexpected differences?
options: A. Back-to-back testing.
B. Data representativeness testing only.
C. Model documentation review only.
D. Label correctness testing only.
answer: A. Back-to-back testing.

Correct! Back-to-back testing compares outputs from the old and new implementations for the same or equivalent inputs. It can reveal unexpected differences without requiring an independently known correct answer for every input, provided a suitable comparison oracle or equivalence criterion is available.
Incorrect! Representativeness testing examines the suitability and coverage of the data. It does not directly compare the behavior of two implementations.
Incorrect! Documentation review can identify relevant assumptions and expected behavior, but it does not replace executing both implementations and comparing their outputs.
Incorrect! Label correctness testing assesses whether labels are correct. It does not directly compare two model implementations.

question: Which statements correctly distinguish A/B testing from back-to-back testing? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. A/B testing compares variants using predefined metrics to evaluate differences in outcomes.
B. Back-to-back testing compares outputs from different implementations or versions using the same or equivalent inputs.
C. Both approaches can help identify problems when an ML model is changed or replaced.
D. Back-to-back testing always proves which implementation is objectively correct, even when no reference behavior is known.
E. A/B testing requires both variants to produce identical predictions.
answer: A. A/B testing compares variants using predefined metrics to evaluate differences in outcomes.
B. Back-to-back testing compares outputs from different implementations or versions using the same or equivalent inputs.
C. Both approaches can help identify problems when an ML model is changed or replaced.

explaination.A. A/B testing compares variants using p: Correct! A/B testing focuses on comparing outcomes or performance measures for different variants using an appropriate experimental and statistical approach.
explaination.B. Back-to-back testing compares outputs: Correct! The central idea is to compare implementations or versions under comparable input conditions and investigate unexpected differences.
explaination.C. Both approaches can help identify pro: Correct! A/B testing can reveal performance degradation or improvement, while back-to-back testing can expose behavioral differences between versions.
explaination.D. Back-to-back testing always proves wh: Incorrect! A difference between outputs does not establish which output is correct. Testers still need appropriate expectations, a reference implementation, a justified equivalence criterion, or further investigation.
