explaination.E. A/B testing requires both variants to: Incorrect! A/B testing is used to compare variants, which may intentionally produce different predictions or outcomes. The goal is to assess the significance and desirability of those differences.

question: A model's performance is acceptable during initial testing. Several months after deployment, monitoring indicates a significant increase in prediction errors. The input data distribution has also changed. Which actions are MOST appropriate? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. Investigate whether data drift or concept drift explains the degradation.
B. Compare current operational behavior with suitable historical or reference data.
C. Evaluate whether retraining or another corrective action is justified by the evidence.
D. Assume that the original acceptance test guarantees continued operational performance.
E. Delete all historical monitoring data before investigating the degradation.
answer: A. Investigate whether data drift or concept drift explains the degradation.
B. Compare current operational behavior with suitable historical or reference data.
C. Evaluate whether retraining or another corrective action is justified by the evidence.

explaination.A. Investigate whether data drift or con: Correct! A change in input distributions may indicate data drift, while a change in input-outcome relationships may indicate concept drift. Either can contribute to reduced performance.
explaination.B. Compare current operational behavior: Correct! Comparisons with appropriate reference distributions and performance measurements help establish what has changed and how significant the degradation is.
explaination.C. Evaluate whether retraining or anothe: Correct! Once the cause and significance of the problem are understood, the team can assess whether retraining, data improvements, model replacement, or another intervention is appropriate.
explaination.D. Assume that the original acceptance t: Incorrect! Initial acceptance testing reflects the conditions and evidence available at that time. Operational conditions can change, so ongoing monitoring is necessary.
explaination.E. Delete all historical monitoring data: Incorrect! Historical monitoring data is valuable evidence for understanding trends and identifying changes. Deleting it would hinder investigation.

question: A model produces an accurate classification for a source image. A tester creates a follow-up image by slightly changing the image brightness. The model's prediction is expected to remain unchanged because the brightness change is within the supported operating conditions. Which statements are CORRECT? (Choose TWO answers.)
options: A. The follow-up image is derived using a transformation that defines a metamorphic test case.
B. The expected relationship is invariance: the prediction should remain unchanged.
C. The test is invalid because metamorphic testing only permits transformations that change the expected output.
D. The test proves that the model is robust against every possible image transformation.
E. The test is a form of data provenance testing because the image has been modified.
answer: A. The follow-up image is derived using a transformation that defines a metamorphic test case.
B. The expected relationship is invariance: the prediction should remain unchanged.

explaination.A. The follow-up image is derived using: Correct! A transformed version of a source input can be used as a follow-up test case when the transformation is associated with a defined metamorphic relation.
explaination.B. The expected relationship is invarian: Correct! The test expects the prediction to remain stable under a transformation that should not affect the classification within the supported operating conditions.
explaination.C. The test is invalid because metamorph: Incorrect! Metamorphic relations may require outputs to remain unchanged or to change in a predictable way. Invariance is a valid relationship.
explaination.D. The test proves that the model is rob: Incorrect! A single test establishes evidence only for the particular transformation and conditions tested. It cannot prove robustness against every possible transformation.
explaination.E. The test is a form of data provenance: Incorrect! Data provenance testing investigates the origin and history of data. Transforming an image to check an expected relationship between outputs is a metamorphic testing approach.

question: A team has limited access to the internal workings of a machine learning model. It wants to investigate whether unexpected inputs cause unstable or incorrect behavior. Which testing approaches are relevant? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. Exploratory testing.
B. Adversarial testing.
C. Fuzz testing.
D. Documentation review as the only activity, without executing the model.
E. Assuming that black-box models cannot be tested.
answer: A. Exploratory testing.
B. Adversarial testing.
C. Fuzz testing.

Correct! Exploratory testing can uncover unexpected behaviors by investigating model responses to different inputs, scenarios, and edge cases.
Correct! Adversarial testing can investigate whether deliberately crafted inputs exploit weaknesses. It can be conducted using black-box observations as well as white-box information.
Correct! Fuzz testing supplies varied, unexpected, or malformed inputs to discover robustness problems and other defects. It is particularly useful when input handling may fail under unusual conditions.
explaination.D. Documentation review as the only acti: Incorrect! Documentation review is useful but does not replace execution-based testing when the objective is to observe the model's response to unexpected inputs.
explaination.E. Assuming that black-box models cannot: Incorrect! Black-box testing is possible using inputs and observable outputs. Limited access to internal details may affect the available techniques, but it does not make testing impossible.

question: Which statements correctly describe the scope of machine learning development testing? (Choose TWO answers.)
options: A. It addresses risks introduced by ML development tools, configuration choices, and deployment mechanisms.
B. It focuses exclusively on the accuracy of the trained model, regardless of the development environment.
C. It includes testing whether an ML system functions correctly and reliably in its target environment.
D. It replaces all input data testing and model testing.
E. It is only concerned with checking whether the source code compiles.
answer: A. It addresses risks introduced by ML development tools, configuration choices, and deployment mechanisms.
C. It includes testing whether an ML system functions correctly and reliably in its target environment.

explaination.A. It addresses risks introduced by ML d: Correct! Section 7.1 of the ISTQB CT-AI v2.0 syllabus focuses on risks arising from ML development tools, configuration choices, and deployment mechanisms.
explaination.B. It focuses exclusively on the accurac: Incorrect! Development testing covers more than predictive accuracy. It also addresses framework suitability, installation, configuration, interfaces, deployment compatibility, and operational behavior.
explaination.C. It includes testing whether an ML sys: Correct! Deployment testing verifies that the ML system functions correctly and reliably in its intended environment, such as a cloud platform, mobile device, or edge device.
explaination.D. It replaces all input data testing an: Incorrect! Development testing complements input data testing and model testing. Each addresses different risks in the ML lifecycle.
explaination.E. It is only concerned with checking wh: Incorrect! Compilation is only one possible aspect of development verification. The syllabus also covers functional performance, security, framework suitability, and deployment testing.

question: A development team discovers that it has used a machine learning framework API incorrectly, resulting in unintended behavior during model training. Which testing approach is MOST directly relevant to detecting this problem?
options: A. API testing.
B. Cross-device testing.
C. Shadow testing.
D. Rollback testing.
answer: A. API testing.

Correct! The syllabus identifies incorrect or unintended use of library or framework APIs, such as TensorFlow or PyTorch APIs, as a development risk that can be mitigated through API testing.
Incorrect! Cross-device testing checks whether the ML system performs correctly across its intended deployment targets. It does not directly address incorrect use of a development framework API.
Incorrect! Shadow testing runs a new model alongside the current production model using live requests without allowing the new model to affect live responses. It is not the primary approach for detecting incorrect API usage during development.
Incorrect! Rollback testing verifies that a system can return to a previously stable state after a failed or degraded deployment.

question: A company is selecting a machine learning framework for a new computer vision application. The team is concerned that its chosen framework may not be appropriate for the application's technical requirements. Which testing activity is MOST appropriate?
options: A. Framework suitability review.
B. Rollback testing.
C. Label correctness testing.
D. Canary testing.
answer: A. Framework suitability review.

Correct! The syllabus identifies framework suitability review as an appropriate mitigation for suboptimal framework selection. The review should assess whether the framework meets the application's requirements.
Incorrect! Rollback testing checks the ability to restore a previously stable system state after a failed or degraded deployment. It does not directly assess framework selection.
Incorrect! Label correctness testing investigates whether the target labels in a dataset are accurate and consistent.
Incorrect! Canary testing evaluates a new deployment using a small subset of production traffic. It does not directly determine whether the selected development framework is suitable.

question: An ML development framework calculates evaluation metrics incorrectly because of a defect in its evaluation implementation. Which testing approaches are MOST appropriate for mitigating this risk? (Choose TWO answers.)
options: A. Review the framework's evaluation code.
B. Cross-check the framework's evaluation results against independent manual benchmarks.
C. Perform rollback testing only.
D. Perform cross-device testing only.
E. Perform label correctness testing only.
answer: A. Review the framework's evaluation code.
B. Cross-check the framework's evaluation results against independent manual benchmarks.

explaination.A. Review the framework's evaluation cod: Correct! The syllabus identifies reviews of framework evaluation code as a mitigation for defects in the framework's evaluation implementation.
explaination.B. Cross-check the framework's evaluatio: Correct! Independent benchmarks can reveal discrepancies between the framework's results and independently established expected results.
Incorrect! Rollback testing checks recovery from failed or degraded deployments. It does not directly validate the correctness of evaluation calculations.
Incorrect! Cross-device testing checks behavior across deployment targets. It does not directly establish whether evaluation metrics are calculated correctly.
explaination.E. Perform label correctness testing onl: Incorrect! Label correctness testing checks dataset labels. Correct labels do not guarantee that the framework calculates evaluation metrics correctly.

question: A machine learning framework responds too slowly during training and evaluation, reducing the efficiency of the development workflow. Which testing approach is MOST directly relevant to investigating this problem?
options: A. Performance testing.
B. Usability testing.
C. Label correctness testing.
D. Data representativeness testing.
answer: A. Performance testing.

Correct! The syllabus identifies poor performance efficiency, such as a framework being slow to respond, as a risk that can be mitigated through performance testing.
Incorrect! Usability testing investigates how easily users can interact with a framework. It does not directly measure processing speed or response time.
Incorrect! Label correctness testing investigates whether labels assigned to training examples are accurate and consistent.
Incorrect! Data representativeness testing checks whether a dataset adequately represents the intended population and operating conditions.

question: A team is concerned that a machine learning framework's interface is difficult for developers to understand and use, leading to frequent configuration mistakes. Which testing approach is MOST appropriate for investigating the framework's usability?
options: A. Usability testing.
B. Security testing.
C. Drift testing.
D. Model conversion testing.
answer: A. Usability testing.

Correct! The syllabus identifies poor usability of an ML development framework as a risk that can be mitigated through usability testing.
Incorrect! Security testing investigates vulnerabilities that could compromise confidentiality, integrity, availability, or other security objectives. It is not the primary approach for assessing interface usability.
Incorrect! Drift testing investigates changes in operational input distributions or relationships between inputs and outputs over time.
Incorrect! Model conversion testing verifies that a model retains acceptable predictive accuracy, behavior, and operational efficiency after conversion to a deployment format.

question: A team suspects that a defect in a third-party library used by its ML framework is affecting predictions. Which approach is explicitly identified in the syllabus as a mitigation for defects in libraries used by a framework?
options: A. ML functional performance testing.
B. Label correctness testing.
C. Installability testing only.
D. Data provenance testing only.
answer: A. ML functional performance testing.

Correct! The syllabus lists ML functional performance testing as a mitigation for a defect in a library used by the framework, such as a defect in PyTorch. It helps assess whether the resulting model behavior meets performance expectations.
Incorrect! Label correctness testing investigates inaccurate or inconsistent labels. It does not directly validate the functional performance of a model affected by a library defect.
Incorrect! Installability testing checks whether the ML system can be installed, configured, and uninstalled successfully across supported environments. It does not directly establish the effect of a library defect on model predictions.
Incorrect! Data provenance testing investigates the origin and history of data. It does not directly establish whether a third-party library defect affects model performance.

question: A model's algorithm implementation may contain defects. The development team wants to compare its behavior against an independent implementation using equivalent inputs. Which testing approach is MOST appropriate?
options: A. Back-to-back testing.
B. Usability testing.
C. Installability testing.
D. Dataset constraint testing.
answer: A. Back-to-back testing.

Correct! Back-to-back testing compares outputs from different implementations or versions using the same or equivalent inputs. The syllabus identifies it as a mitigation for defective algorithm implementations.
Incorrect! Usability testing assesses how easily people can interact with a system or framework. It does not directly compare algorithm outputs.
Incorrect! Installability testing checks whether the system can be installed, configured, and uninstalled in supported environments.
Incorrect! Dataset constraint testing verifies that records satisfy predefined rules, such as data types, ranges, uniqueness, and required fields.

question: Which risk-to-mitigation mappings are CORRECT according to the ISTQB CT-AI v2.0 syllabus? (Choose FOUR answers.)
options: A. Security vulnerabilities in the framework — security testing.
B. Poor user documentation for the framework — framework documentation review.
C. Defective allocation of data to training, validation, and testing datasets — data allocation review.
D. Suboptimal framework selection — framework suitability review.
E. Defective framework installation or build — shadow testing.
F. Problems introducing systemic unfairness — installability testing.
answer: A. Security vulnerabilities in the framework — security testing.
B. Poor user documentation for the framework — framework documentation review.
C. Defective allocation of data to training, validation, and testing datasets — data allocation review.
D. Suboptimal framework selection — framework suitability review.

explaination.A. Security vulnerabilities in the frame: Correct! Security testing is explicitly identified as an approach for mitigating security vulnerabilities in an ML development framework.
explaination.B. Poor user documentation for the frame: Correct! Reviewing framework documentation can identify missing, unclear, or inadequate guidance that creates development risks.
explaination.C. Defective allocation of data to train: Correct! A data allocation review checks whether the datasets have been assigned appropriately for their intended roles.
explaination.D. Suboptimal framework selection — fram: Correct! Framework suitability review investigates whether the selected framework meets the requirements of the application.
explaination.E. Defective framework installation or b: Incorrect! The syllabus identifies smoke testing as a mitigation for a defective framework installation or build. Shadow testing is a deployment technique that runs a new model alongside the current production model.
explaination.F. Problems introducing systemic unfairn: Incorrect! Testing for bias is the appropriate mitigation for problems in the algorithm, model, or development framework that introduce systemic unfairness. Installability testing checks successful installation, configuration, and uninstallation.

question: A team has generated a model for deployment on a target platform using a different model format from the original training format. Which testing activity is MOST appropriate for verifying that conversion has not introduced unacceptable problems?
options: A. Model conversion testing.
B. Data provenance testing.
C. Label correctness testing.
D. Usability testing of the development framework.
answer: A. Model conversion testing.

Correct! Model conversion testing verifies that predictive accuracy, behavior, and operational efficiency remain acceptable after conversion to a format suitable for the target production environment.
Incorrect! Data provenance testing investigates where data originated and how it was handled. It does not directly validate the effects of converting a model format.
Incorrect! Label correctness testing assesses whether dataset labels are accurate and consistent. It does not directly verify that a converted model retains its expected behavior.
explaination.D. Usability testing of the development: Incorrect! Usability testing investigates how easily users can interact with the development framework. It does not directly verify model conversion.

question: A model is converted from its original training format into an optimized format for deployment. Which properties should be checked during model conversion testing? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. Acceptable predictive accuracy.
B. Consistent model behavior.
C. Operational efficiency, such as inference speed and memory usage.
D. The number of developers who contributed to the original model.
E. Whether the training dataset contains a unique identifier for every record, regardless of the application's requirements.
answer: A. Acceptable predictive accuracy.
B. Consistent model behavior.
C. Operational efficiency, such as inference speed and memory usage.

Correct! Conversion should not reduce predictive accuracy below acceptable requirements.
Correct! The converted model should behave consistently with the intended behavior of the original model under comparable conditions.
explaination.C. Operational efficiency, such as infer: Correct! Model conversion testing also considers operational efficiency, including inference speed and memory consumption.
explaination.D. The number of developers who contribu: Incorrect! Developer count is not a property that model conversion testing is intended to verify.
explaination.E. Whether the training dataset contains: Incorrect! Dataset identifier requirements are a separate data quality concern. They are not a primary objective of model conversion testing.

question: A company deploys an ML system to mobile devices, edge devices, and cloud servers. It wants to verify that the system works correctly across all supported deployment targets. Which testing approach is MOST appropriate?
options: A. Cross-device testing.
B. Shadow testing.
C. Rollback testing.
D. Framework documentation review.
answer: A. Cross-device testing.

Correct! Cross-device testing verifies that the ML system performs correctly across its intended range of deployment targets, from mobile and edge devices to cloud servers.
Incorrect! Shadow testing runs a new model alongside the existing production model using the same live requests without affecting live responses. It does not specifically address compatibility across device types.
Incorrect! Rollback testing verifies the ability to return to a previously stable and operational state after a degraded or failed deployment.
Incorrect! Documentation review assesses the quality and completeness of framework documentation. It does not directly verify execution across supported devices.

question: A new model must be installed on a supported edge device. The team needs to verify that installation scripts run correctly, required GPU drivers are available, dependencies are compatible, and the model can subsequently be uninstalled. Which testing approach is MOST appropriate?
options: A. Installability testing.
B. Canary testing.
C. A/B testing.
D. Metamorphic testing.
answer: A. Installability testing.

Correct! Installability testing verifies successful installation, configuration, and uninstallation across supported environments. It includes checking dependencies, framework compatibility, and installation scripts.
Incorrect! Canary testing releases an updated model to a small subset of production traffic and monitors metrics before a wider rollout.
Incorrect! A/B testing compares two variants using predefined metrics and appropriate statistical analysis. It does not directly validate installation scripts or dependencies.
Incorrect! Metamorphic testing checks expected relationships between outputs from related test inputs. It does not directly validate installation and uninstallation.

question: A model deployment fails after a new version introduces unacceptable latency. The team wants to verify that it can restore the previous stable version and, if necessary, restore the associated data pipeline. Which testing approach is MOST appropriate?
options: A. Rollback testing.
B. Installability testing only.
C. Cross-device testing.
D. Label correctness testing.
answer: A. Rollback testing.

Correct! Rollback testing verifies that the system can return to a previously stable state following a degraded or failed deployment. It can cover only the model or the complete system, including the data pipeline. The syllabus states that rollback readiness must be tested before deployment.
Incorrect! Installability testing verifies installation, configuration, and uninstallation. It does not by itself demonstrate that the system can recover to a previous stable version.
Incorrect! Cross-device testing checks correct operation across supported deployment targets. It does not directly verify recovery after a failed deployment.
Incorrect! Label correctness testing assesses the accuracy and consistency of dataset labels. It does not verify rollback capability.

question: A company wants to deploy a new ML model to production while limiting the impact of potential defects. The company routes 5% of production traffic to the new model, monitors latency, accuracy, and error rates, and expands the rollout if the results are acceptable. Which deployment testing approach is being used?
options: A. Canary testing.
B. Shadow testing.
C. Back-to-back testing.
D. Installability testing.
answer: A. Canary testing.

Correct! Canary testing releases an updated model to a small subset of production traffic, such as 5% of users, and monitors real-time metrics to detect regressions before full rollout.
Incorrect! Shadow testing sends the same requests to a new model and the current production model in parallel, but the new model's responses do not affect live responses. The scenario explicitly routes real production traffic to the new model.
Incorrect! Back-to-back testing compares outputs from two implementations or versions for the same or equivalent inputs to detect defects. It does not inherently involve gradually routing a small proportion of live traffic to a new model.
Incorrect! Installability testing verifies successful installation, configuration, and uninstallation in supported environments.

question: A new fraud detection model must be evaluated using real production requests before it is allowed to influence customer transactions. The current production model continues to determine the actual responses. Which testing approach is MOST appropriate?
options: A. Shadow testing.
B. Canary testing.
C. Rollback testing.
D. Installability testing.
answer: A. Shadow testing.

Correct! Shadow testing runs the new model in parallel with the current production model, routing the same requests to both without allowing the new model to affect live responses. This enables comparison using real operational data while limiting deployment risk.
Incorrect! Canary testing allows an updated model to handle a small subset of actual production traffic. In the stated scenario, the current model must continue determining live responses.
Incorrect! Rollback testing verifies the ability to restore a previous stable state following a failed or degraded deployment.
Incorrect! Installability testing verifies that the ML system can be installed, configured, and uninstalled across supported environments.

question: Which statements correctly distinguish shadow testing from canary testing? (Choose THREE answers.)
options: A. Shadow testing runs the new model alongside the current production model using the same requests.
B. In shadow testing, the new model's responses do not affect live responses.
C. Canary testing releases an updated model to a small subset of production traffic and monitors its behavior.
D. Shadow testing and canary testing always route the same percentage of users to the new model.
E. Canary testing requires the new model to remain completely isolated from all production requests.
answer: A. Shadow testing runs the new model alongside the current production model using the same requests.
B. In shadow testing, the new model's responses do not affect live responses.
C. Canary testing releases an updated model to a small subset of production traffic and monitors its behavior.

explaination.A. Shadow testing runs the new model alo: Correct! The defining feature of shadow testing is that both models receive the same live requests in parallel.
explaination.B. In shadow testing, the new model's re: Correct! The current production model continues to determine the actual responses, allowing the new model to be evaluated without directly affecting users.
explaination.C. Canary testing releases an updated mo: Correct! Canary testing limits the initial exposure of a new deployment and uses monitored metrics to identify regressions before a broader rollout.
explaination.D. Shadow testing and canary testing alw: Incorrect! Shadow testing mirrors requests to the new model without allowing its output to affect live responses. Canary testing routes a subset of actual production traffic to the new version. Their traffic handling differs.
explaination.E. Canary testing requires the new model: Incorrect! Canary testing specifically exposes the new model to a small subset of production traffic. A model that receives mirrored requests without influencing live responses is characteristic of shadow testing.

question: A deployed ML service exposes an API to external applications. The team wants to verify that the service correctly handles valid and invalid requests, returns appropriate outputs and error messages, and integrates correctly with upstream data feeds. Which testing approach is MOST appropriate?
options: A. API testing.
B. Model conversion testing.
C. Cross-device testing.
D. Rollback testing.
answer: A. API testing.

Correct! The syllabus states that API testing verifies well-defined, standards-compliant interfaces and checks input and output handling, error messages, and integration workflows with external systems.
Incorrect! Model conversion testing checks whether a converted model retains acceptable predictive accuracy, consistent behavior, and operational efficiency.
Incorrect! Cross-device testing verifies correct operation across supported deployment targets, such as mobile devices, edge devices, and cloud servers.
Incorrect! Rollback testing verifies the ability to restore a previous stable system state after a failed or degraded deployment.

question: Which deployment testing approach is MOST appropriate for each of the following risks? (Choose FOUR answers.)
options: A. The model cannot be installed because a required dependency is missing — installability testing.
B. The system cannot restore a stable version after a failed deployment — rollback testing.
C. A converted model has unacceptable inference latency — model conversion testing.
D. A new model must be evaluated on real production requests without affecting live responses — shadow testing.
E. The new model should receive a small percentage of live traffic before full rollout — rollback testing.
F. The model behaves incorrectly on supported mobile devices — label correctness testing.
answer: A. The model cannot be installed because a required dependency is missing — installability testing.
B. The system cannot restore a stable version after a failed deployment — rollback testing.
C. A converted model has unacceptable inference latency — model conversion testing.
D. A new model must be evaluated on real production requests without affecting live responses — shadow testing.

explaination.A. The model cannot be installed because: Correct! Installability testing checks installation scripts, dependencies, framework compatibility, configuration, and successful installation and uninstallation.
explaination.B. The system cannot restore a stable ve: Correct! Rollback testing verifies recovery to a previously stable and operational state following a failed or degraded deployment.
explaination.C. A converted model has unacceptable in: Correct! Model conversion testing checks whether conversion preserves operational efficiency, including inference speed and memory usage, as well as acceptable accuracy and behavior.
explaination.D. A new model must be evaluated on real: Correct! Shadow testing sends the same live requests to both the existing model and the new model while keeping the new model's outputs from affecting actual responses.
explaination.E. The new model should receive a small: Incorrect! This scenario describes canary testing. Canary testing exposes a small subset of production traffic to the new model and monitors its behavior before expanding the rollout.
explaination.F. The model behaves incorrectly on supp: Incorrect! Cross-device testing is the appropriate approach for verifying model behavior across supported devices. Label correctness testing evaluates the accuracy and consistency of dataset labels.

question: A new ML model has been deployed, but the team is concerned that it may not improve on the current production model. The team wants to evaluate the new model using live operational requests before deciding whether to replace the current model. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
options: A. Shadow testing.
B. Dataset constraint testing.
C. Label correctness testing.
D. Installability testing only.
answer: A. Shadow testing.

Correct! The syllabus identifies shadow testing as a mitigation for the risk that a deployed model is no improvement over the current model. It allows the new model to be compared with the current production model using live requests without affecting live responses.
Incorrect! Dataset constraint testing verifies that data satisfies predefined rules, such as valid types, ranges, and uniqueness. It does not directly compare the deployed model with the current production model.
Incorrect! Label correctness testing investigates whether labels are accurate and consistent. It does not directly evaluate whether the new deployed model improves on the current model.
Incorrect! Installability testing checks whether the model can be installed, configured, and uninstalled. Successful installation does not demonstrate that the new model improves on the current model.

question: A team deploys an ML system to a new cloud environment. The model's predictions are mostly unchanged, but the new environment causes increased memory usage and inference latency. Which statements are CORRECT? (Choose TWO answers.)
options: A. Deployment testing should verify that the system functions correctly and reliably in the target environment.
B. Model conversion testing may be relevant if the model was converted into a format intended for the new environment.
C. Predictive accuracy is the only property that needs to be checked during deployment.
D. Cross-device testing is irrelevant whenever a system is deployed to a cloud environment.
E. Successful installation proves that inference latency and memory usage are acceptable.
answer: A. Deployment testing should verify that the system functions correctly and reliably in the target environment.
B. Model conversion testing may be relevant if the model was converted into a format intended for the new environment.

explaination.A. Deployment testing should verify that: Correct! Deployment testing assesses whether the ML system operates correctly and reliably in its intended environment. This includes investigating relevant operational problems.
explaination.B. Model conversion testing may be relev: Correct! If conversion occurred, model conversion testing can assess whether the converted model retains acceptable predictive accuracy, behavior, and efficiency, including inference speed and memory usage.
explaination.C. Predictive accuracy is the only prope: Incorrect! Deployment quality includes more than predictive accuracy. Relevant aspects include compatibility, reliability, operational efficiency, interfaces, and correct behavior in the target environment.
explaination.D. Cross-device testing is irrelevant wh: Incorrect! Cross-device testing applies to the intended range of deployment targets, including cloud servers. It is relevant whenever the system must operate across multiple supported target types.
explaination.E. Successful installation proves that i: Incorrect! Successful installation does not establish acceptable performance. Latency and memory usage require appropriate performance evaluation.

question: A model developer reports that a new model achieves better accuracy than the current model during training. Before replacing the current production model, the team wants evidence that the new model is beneficial under real operational conditions. Which statements are CORRECT? (Choose TWO answers.)
options: A. Shadow testing can compare the new and current models using live requests without affecting live responses.
B. Canary testing can expose a small subset of production traffic to the new model while monitoring its behavior.
C. Higher training accuracy alone proves that the new model will improve production outcomes.
D. Installability testing alone establishes that the new model is better than the current model.
E. Rollback testing determines which model has the highest predictive accuracy.
answer: A. Shadow testing can compare the new and current models using live requests without affecting live responses.
B. Canary testing can expose a small subset of production traffic to the new model while monitoring its behavior.

explaination.A. Shadow testing can compare the new an: Correct! Shadow testing provides a controlled way to compare the new model with the current production model using real operational requests while preserving the current model's live responses.
explaination.B. Canary testing can expose a small sub: Correct! Canary testing evaluates a new model under limited production exposure and monitors metrics before a full rollout.
explaination.C. Higher training accuracy alone proves: Incorrect! Training accuracy does not establish production performance or generalization. Evaluation on appropriate data and controlled deployment testing provide additional evidence.
explaination.D. Installability testing alone establis: Incorrect! Installability testing verifies installation, configuration, and uninstallation. It does not establish comparative predictive performance.
explaination.E. Rollback testing determines which mod: Incorrect! Rollback testing verifies recovery to a previously stable state. Comparing predictive accuracy requires appropriate model evaluation or comparison techniques.
